sections.title: 2. Who the exam is for
sections.html:
As a candidate for this Microsoft Certification, you’re a professional developer or advanced builder who builds, extends, and integrates custom agents for enterprise-grade solutions. You typically work as an IT application developer, consultant, or independent software vendor (ISV) partner focused on creating scalable AI solutions for organizations or customers.

For this exam, you should be familiar with Power Fx, Microsoft Dataverse, Microsoft Power Platform environments and components, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Foundry, and adaptive cards.

You need intermediate knowledge of generative AI concepts, including models, orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, and more. You should also have experience with prompt engineering and with REST APIs and integration patterns. Additionally, you need experience configuring agents with basic knowledge sources, instructions, tools, and topics in Microsoft Copilot Studio.

As a developer who works in Copilot Studio, you:

  • Integrate agents with Microsoft Foundry.
  • Integrate agents with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
  • Integrate agents with custom connectors.
  • Integrate agents with APIs.
  • Integrate agents with Microsoft Fabric.
  • Automate tasks with computer use.
  • Integrate agents with connectors.

You create:

  • Multi-agent solutions.
  • Agents with enterprise knowledge sources (such as ServiceNow, SAP, and others).
  • Advanced agent topics and tools.
  • Computer-using agents.
  • Agents that perform advanced actions via APIs.

You collaborate with Microsoft 365 administrators, Microsoft Power Platform administrators, Microsoft Copilot administrators, Copilot Studio agent builders, Copilot Studio administrators, Foundry administrators, agentic AI business solutions architects, and Copilot Studio architects.

Source: Official study guide (audience profile), updated 2026-10-16.

sections.title: 1.1 Plan an agent solution
sections.html:
Skills measured: Plan integration with enterprise systems • Plan identity strategy • Plan channels and deployment • Plan responsible AI strategy • Evaluate security and governance considerations • Plan reuseable agent components • Design agents for internal or external audiences. Practise by taking one scenario (for example a ServiceNow or SAP service-desk agent) and writing down, for each of the seven topics, the option you would choose and the rule that rules out the alternatives.

Vocabulary used by AB-620

Agent flows, topics, tools and generative answers belong to the standard harness (the classic experience); the GitHub Copilot harness has workflows instead. Renames you will meet in older material: “Respond to Copilot” is now Respond to the agent; “Actions” and the “Library” are now Tools; Microsoft Graph connectors are now Copilot connectors; messages are now Copilot Credits; Azure AI Foundry is now Microsoft Foundry.

Plan integration with enterprise systems

Start from the system (ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce, SQL, Dataverse, an internal API), then decide knowledge or action, how the caller authenticates, the expected volume and the network path. The patterns are not exclusive and are often combined. An integration is attached as a tool (the orchestrator chooses it), as a topic node (fixed position, Power Fx inputs) or as an agent (child or connected).

PatternUse whenWatch out for
Prebuilt Power Platform connectorA connector already exists for the systemStandard connectors work on all plans, Premium on select plans; ServiceNow and SAP OData are Premium
Custom connectorNo prebuilt connector; wrap any public REST API once and reuse it in many agentsMust be shared before other makers can use it
HTTP request nodeOne-off call that must be built quicklyYou enter URI, method, headers and body each time; it can't be shared for reuse
Agent flowDeterministic multi-step process, secrets from Azure Key Vault, large data or files, converting existing cloud flowsYou must design error handling; the response to the agent has a size limit
Bot Framework skillPro-code (C#) logic, private endpointsExtra Azure cost; ALM outside Power Platform
Computer useNo API, only a user interfaceBilled at the agent-action rate

Copilot connectors or Power Platform connectors for knowledge?

Copilot connectors (formerly Graph connectors)Power Platform connectors
MechanismIndex external content into Microsoft Graph (data is copied, source ACLs are honoured)Call the API in real time under the user's connection; no data movement
Best forLarge bodies of content (ServiceNow knowledge base, Jira, Confluence, GitHub, Azure DevOps) that need semantic search, citations and reuse across Microsoft 365 CopilotLive answers (“What's the status of ticket 1234?”), create or update transactions, no replication
Set upAdmin connects the source in the Microsoft 365 admin center; in Copilot Studio use Add knowledge; manual authentication needs the ExternalItem.Read.All scope when you publish to channelsMaker or admin creates the connection; data policies govern it; as knowledge it is Preview (Add knowledge → Advanced → real-time connector)
  • Plan each integration: connected system, caller, inputs, daily and peak volume, API calls per minute, and the Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Power Platform request and per-connector limits. If flows or connectors are too slow, consider Dataverse custom APIs, low-code plug-ins or Azure Functions.
  • Private network: Virtual Network support requires a Managed Environment (Azure Key Vault through HTTP, private-endpoint Application Insights, VNet-supported connectors such as SQL Server). MCP servers need generative orchestration, and blocking Power Platform connectors in a data policy also blocks MCP tools.
Exam traps
  • “Fresh status without copying” means a Power Platform connector; “cited answers across Microsoft 365 Copilot” means a Copilot connector.
  • An HTTP request node is rebuilt in every agent; only a custom connector is reusable.
  • Real-time knowledge from Power Platform connectors is Preview and indexes only metadata (table and column names). “Graph connectors” is the old name of Copilot connectors.

Plan identity strategy

Plan three identities: the end user, the credentials each tool uses and the agent's own identity. User authentication lives under Settings → Security → Authentication; changes take effect only after you publish.

OptionWhat it gives youTopic variables
No authenticationAnyone with the link can chat and you can't restrict users by sharing. Tools can't use user credentials. Not selectable when a data policy requires authentication.—
Authenticate with Microsoft (default for new agents)Entra ID sign-in with no setup for Teams, Power Apps and Microsoft Copilot; Require users to sign in is always on; sharing controls who can chat; not available with Dynamics 365 Customer Service hand-offUser.ID, User.DisplayName only
Authenticate manuallyFor channels beyond Teams and Microsoft 365. Providers: Entra ID V2 with federated credentials (recommended), with certificates or with client secrets; Microsoft Entra ID; Generic OAuth 2 (any OAuth2 provider, such as Google or Facebook)User.Id, User.DisplayName, User.AccessToken, User.IsLoggedIn
  • Sharing as access control works with Authenticate with Microsoft and with manual Microsoft Entra ID when Require users to sign in is on; it can't restrict No authentication or manual Generic OAuth 2.
  • Require users to sign in creates a read-only system topic of the same name (it redirects to Escalate if sign-in fails); with it off, sign-in is requested only when a topic needs it.

Manual authentication with federated credentials

  1. Azure portal → App registrations → New registration (single tenant); copy the Application (client) ID.
  2. Authentication → Add a platform → Web; redirect URI https://token.botframework.com/.auth/web/redirect; select Access tokens and ID tokens.
  3. Copilot Studio → Authenticate manually, leave Require users to sign in on, provider Microsoft Entra ID V2 with federated credentials, paste the client ID, Save, then copy the federated credential issuer and value.
  4. Azure portal → Certificates & secrets → Federated credentials → Add credential → Other issuer; paste issuer and value.
  5. Grant admin consent under API permissions, then publish.
  • Tool credentials: per tool (Details → Additional details → Authentication): End user (default; a Connect card appears when the user has no connection) or Maker-provided. User credentials work on channels that authenticate users (custom website, Teams, SharePoint, Omnichannel live chat), not on the Demo website, Facebook, the mobile app or Azure Bot Service channels.
  • Admin control: admin center → Manage → Environments or Environment groups → Settings → Product → Features → Copilot Studio agents → Control maker credential options (end-user, maker-provided or both; default both). Turning maker-provided off applies immediately to every tool. Needs Environment Admin (one environment) or Power Platform administrator (groups).
  • SSO: Teams signs users in silently; a custom website needs two app registrations (authentication and canvas) and the Token exchange URL.
  • Agent identity: each new agent automatically gets a Microsoft Entra Agent ID (a service principal; older agents keep legacy app registrations; see Settings → Advanced → Metadata). Publishing attaches connector scopes (Operations.Execute.All, per-operation scopes or Azure API Connections Runtime.All); Conditional Access on the agent identity is currently enforced only in Teams.
Exam traps
  • Authenticate with Microsoft exposes no access token and no User.IsLoggedIn; topics that use them show Unknown variables after a switch. Watch the casing User.ID versus User.Id.
  • No authentication and “tool runs with the user's credentials” contradict each other.
  • Maker-provided credentials can over-share data; the admin switch applies at once and forces end-user sign-in prompts.

Plan channels and deployment

  • Publishing: publish at least once before adding channels; one publish updates all connected channels; republish after every change. New content reaches users in a new session: sessions end after 30 minutes of inactivity in most channels. In persistent channels (Teams, Omnichannel) type start over to test at once; otherwise the new version can take up to one hour.
ChannelUse it for / note
Teams and Microsoft CopilotEmployees; install link or Make the agent available to others; its data-policy connector is still named Microsoft Teams + Microsoft 365 Channel
SharePoint, WhatsApp, Facebook, mobile appDedicated channels, each with its own connection steps
Demo websiteTesting only; share the URL with your team and stakeholders, never with customers
Custom websiteProduction web (iframe or Web Chat); secure it with Direct Line secrets or tokens
Azure Bot Service channels, Power PagesSlack, Telegram, Twilio, Line, Kik, GroupMe, Direct Line Speech, email; Power Pages sites
Dynamics 365 Customer Service (Omnichannel)Live-agent hand-off (or another engagement hub)

Secure the web channels

By default anyone who has the agent ID can reach the Demo and Custom website channels. Turn on Settings → Security → Web channel security → Require secured access so each request carries a Direct Line secret (service-to-service) or a token (browser or mobile code; valid for one conversation). Never put the secret in browser code; exchange it for a token in your own service:

POST https://directline.botframework.com/v3/directline/tokens/generate
Authorization: Bearer <SECRET>

The setting can take up to two hours to take effect and needs no republish. Two secrets exist so you can swap them without downtime.

Govern channels and promote between environments

  • Data policies block channels through connectors (Direct Line channels, Facebook, Omnichannel, SharePoint, WhatsApp, Teams + Microsoft 365); if no channel is allowed the agent can't be published. Agent access channels (admin center → Security → Identity and access) is Preview.
  • ALM: at least three environments (development, test, production); production is a production-type environment, the others sandbox; one Entra security group per environment; carry agents in solutions exported as managed, with environment variables and connection references for environment-specific values.
  • Not solution-aware (redo after deployment): Application Insights settings, manual authentication settings, Direct Line / web channel security settings, deployed channels and sharing.
Exam traps
  • The Demo website is not a production channel, and a Direct Line secret must never reach browser code.
  • “Published but users still see the old behaviour”: the session hasn't restarted (30 minutes idle, or start over).
  • Require secured access needs no publish but can take two hours.
  • Promoting by solution does not move sharing, channels, web-channel security, Application Insights or manual authentication settings.

Plan responsible AI strategy

Microsoft's Responsible AI Standard has six principles: fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency and accountability. The Copilot Studio guidance article frames four core practices (fairness, accountability, transparency, ethics). Planning means choosing a control for each risk:

RiskControlDetail
Harmful or manipulated contentContent moderationApplies to all generative requests and is checked twice (on the input and again before the response); covers jailbreak, prompt injection, prompt exfiltration and copyright. Levels Lowest to Highest, default High, set at agent level (Generative AI settings), topic level (generative answers node) and prompt-tool level; the topic setting wins over the agent setting.
A prompt tool blocks legitimate sensitive textPrompt Content moderation levelLow, Moderate or High; default Moderate; Low suits prompts that process descriptions of violence or medical procedures. Available only for managed models, not Anthropic or Foundry models.
Answers invented from general knowledgeAllow ungrounded responses offWhen on, the agent can answer from the model's general knowledge if it can't cite a source
Irreversible or high-impact actionsConfirmation and approvalsTool setting Ask the end user before running (default No); approval steps in flows (§1.2)
Users unaware they are talking to AIDisclosureDefault message: “Just so you are aware, I sometimes use AI to answer your questions.”; tell users when AI generates questions or answers
  • Orchestration safeguards: the agent uses only the tools and knowledge you configured, admins can restrict tools, classifiers screen user input, trigger data and tool outputs, and blocked content appears as “content filtered” on the activity map.
  • Platform guidance: keep the scope narrow, require approval for high-impact actions, prefer reversible tasks, test in a sandbox, monitor, keep humans in control of finance, healthcare and legal decisions, and evaluate third-party, preview or experimental models yourself.
Exam traps
  • Agent and node moderation default to High; the prompt-tool default is Moderate.
  • Lowering moderation produces more answers and more risk; raising it blocks more.
  • The prompt moderation slider is unavailable for Anthropic and Foundry models.
  • Moderation, grounding and confirmation solve different risks; stricter moderation does not stop an agent from acting without approval.
  • Six Responsible AI principles versus four guidance practices: both appear in the docs.

Evaluate security and governance considerations

Map each risk to the right control and the right scope (tenant, environment or agent).

RiskControlWhere / scope
Anonymous chatBlock Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot StudioData policy: admin center → Security → Data and privacy → Data policy
Exfiltration through knowledge or HTTPBlock the knowledge-source or HTTP connector, or apply endpoint filtering (HTTP, public websites, SharePoint)Data policy
Over-sharingSharing limits; Editor only for individualsManaged Environment, environment group or rules
Maker credentials exposing dataControl maker credential optionsEnvironment or environment group
Key ownershipCustomer-managed keysEnvironment
Private servicesVirtual Network supportManaged Environment
AuditMicrosoft Purview audit (events such as BotCreate, BotUpdateOperation-BotPublish, BotUpdateOperation-BotShare); activity collection can't be disabled, but the audit logs in Purview can be turned offTenant
Attacks at run timeBuilt-in protection; external threat detection Preview through a REST endpoint (custom, Microsoft Defender or others)Agents with generative orchestration
  • Data policies sort connectors into Business, Non-business and Blocked; connectors that exchange data must be in the same group. Enforcement is real time and the old exemption is gone. Copilot Studio connectors include Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication, HTTP, the knowledge-source connectors for documents (local uploads only), SharePoint and OneDrive and public websites, the channel connectors, Skills, and Application Insights.
  • Sharing limits: Editor can be granted only to individuals, never to security groups; the rules apply to agents that require authentication and can take up to an hour to apply.
  • There is no single switch that turns off agent creation. Control authors through licences, security groups and environment roles (environment-level security roles can allow or block creating, reading, updating or deleting agents), and use data policies to stop publishing or chatting.
  • Microsoft Agent 365 is the control plane to observe, govern and secure agents. Customer Lockbox does not cover Purview audit telemetry or Agent 365 events.
  • Zoned governance: Zone 1 citizen (Agent Builder, SharePoint agents), Zone 2 partnered (IT-approved makers, Copilot Studio, pipelines), Zone 3 professional (Foundry Agent Service and Copilot Studio, strongest controls).
Exam traps
  • Blocking the documents knowledge connector stops only local file uploads; SharePoint and OneDrive have their own connector.
  • Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks MCP tools.
  • Sharing limits apply only to agents that require authentication, and Editor can't go to a security group.
  • There is no single tenant switch for agent creation; the levers are data policy plus roles, security groups and licences.

Plan reuseable agent components

Plan reuse at four levels: a component collection (shared building blocks), a solution (the carrier between environments), a shared tool and a connected agent.

GoalUse
Share topics, knowledge, tools, child agents, MCP connections, connectors, flows or entities among agents in one environmentComponent collection
Move collections between environments with independent release cyclesCollection export (managed) or a solution
Collection that contains connectors or environment variablesSolution
One backend capability for many agentsTool on the Tools page (formerly Library); each agent keeps its own wrapper with its own inputs, outputs and configuration
Single-purpose subtask inside one agent, same team, no separate publishingChild agent
Reusable agent with its own publishing, model, ALM or owner, or more than about 30–40 choices (an agent allows up to 128 tools; 25–30 are recommended)Connected agent
  • Create: agent Settings → Component collections (or the sidebar … menu) → Create or New → name and description → select components (dependencies are added automatically) → review → Create. Components move into the collection and the agent references them.
  • Who can edit: to edit a collection or add it to an agent you must be its creator or hold the system customizer or system admin role. Other agent authors can use it but can't change its components. Sharing offers Viewer or Editor.
  • Primary agent: limits a collection to one agent and lets you exclude dependencies; it can be set only while a single agent is connected.
  • Export and import: export creates a managed .zip; import through the agent's Settings → Component collections → Import solution into a different environment (importing into the source environment errors). Uploaded knowledge files move into the collection and leave the originating agent.
  • Also reusable: custom connectors, agent flows (one flow, many agents) and topics with inputs and outputs. HTTP request nodes are not.
Exam traps
  • A child agent is not reusable outside its parent; a connected agent is.
  • “Library” is the old name of the Tools page.
  • Exported collections are managed; use a solution when you need connectors or environment variables.
  • You can't set a primary agent while several agents are connected, and you can't import into the environment you exported from.

Design agents for internal or external audiences

Pick the audience first; it drives authentication, channel, licensing and governance.

AudienceAuthenticationChannelNotes
Employees in Teams or Microsoft CopilotAuthenticate with MicrosoftTeams and Microsoft CopilotSilent SSO; share with security groups
Employees on an intranet siteManual (Entra ID) with SSOCustom websiteTwo app registrations and a token exchange URL
Anonymous public (FAQ)No authenticationCustom websiteNo tools with user credentials; secure the web channel; block risky connectors by data policy
Customers with their own identityManual with Generic OAuth 2Custom website, mobile app, Facebook, WhatsApp, Azure Bot Service channelsHand-off to a person needs Dynamics 365 Customer Service (Omnichannel) or another engagement hub
Users in another tenantAuthenticate with MicrosoftTeams and Microsoft Copilot onlyMultitenant mode Preview
  • Licensing: employee-facing use by Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed users (authenticated with their Copilot identity) carries no Copilot Credits charge for classic answers, generative answers and tenant graph grounding. For agent flows the inclusion applies only to runs started by When an agent calls the flow. A trial licence can't publish.
  • Multitenant mode Preview: an agent hosted in one tenant is used from another; Teams and Microsoft Copilot only, one-on-one chats only; the host tenant builds, hosts and pays. Not supported: end-user authentication, OAuth, guest users, custom connectors, computer use, agent flows and MCP tools; transcripts are off; it is blocked when Power Platform tenant isolation is on.
Exam traps
  • Authenticate with Microsoft can't sign in customers who use Google, Facebook or another OAuth2 provider; that needs manual authentication with Generic OAuth 2.
  • Multitenant mode is Preview and drops agent flows, custom connectors, MCP tools and computer use; guest users aren't supported.
  • Live-agent hand-off is an Omnichannel or engagement-hub feature, not something the agent provides alone.

Sources: Integration guidance · Copilot vs Power Platform connectors · User authentication · Manual Entra authentication · Control maker credentials · Agent identities · Publish channels · Web channel security · ALM guidance · Generative answers and moderation · Prompt model settings · Data policies · Security and governance · Component collections · Multitenant overview · Copilot Credits

sections.title: 1.2 Create and monitor agent flows in Copilot Studio
sections.html:
Skills measured: Create an agent flow • Create a human-in-the-loop agent flow • Configure actions and connectors • Monitor agent flows • Add input and output parameters • Implement error handling in agent flows. Practise by building one agent flow that starts with When an agent calls the flow, asks a person for information, calls a connector and has a Try/Catch scope; call it from an agent as a tool, then break it and read the failed run on the Activity tab.

Create an agent flow

An agent flow is a deterministic flow made of a trigger and at least one action. It is built in Copilot Studio (standard harness) and consumes Copilot Studio capacity for every action it runs. Action categories in the designer: AI capabilities (generate text, process documents, Run a prompt, Run an agent, reply to a calling agent), Human in the loop (approvals, Request for information), Built-in tools (loops, branching, data operations, date and time, child flows) and Connectors (Microsoft 365, third-party, custom).

Do not confuseWhat it is
Agent flowStandard harness; made in Copilot Studio; billed in Copilot Credits; can run prompts, call agents and include human review
Power Automate cloud flowPower Automate licensing; shows in Copilot Studio only after conversion
WorkflowGitHub Copilot harness format; a cloud flow can't be converted into it
  • Natural language: describe the flow in a multi-turn chat (“When X happens, do Y”). It uses Anthropic models, so an admin must allow external models; once opened in the designer, Copilot can't edit it any more.
  • Designer: Insert a new action, Parameters tab, Version history (stored in Dataverse; save once first), Flow checker (errors block publishing, warnings don't), Publish, Test.
  • Convert a Power Automate cloud flow (one-way, and it stays reachable in Power Automate): open its details page in the Power Automate portal → make sure it is in a solution → make sure the environment has Copilot Studio capacity (prepaid or pay-as-you-go) → Edit → change the plan to Copilot Studio → Save → confirm.

Make the flow callable as a tool

RequirementDetail
Trigger and responseWhen an agent calls the flow and Respond to the agent; both are added for you when you create the flow as a tool from the agent or from the Flows page
Real-time responseAsynchronous response = Off (Respond to the agent → Settings → Networking)
TimeRespond within 100 seconds; actions placed after Respond to the agent can keep running up to the 30-day run limit
PackagingA solution flow in the same environment as the agent, and published
Add to the agentAgent → Tools → Add a tool → flow → Add and configure (name, description, inputs, completion) → Save
  • Licence and billing: no Power Automate licence is needed and premium connectors work. Billing is 13 Copilot Credits per 100 agent flow actions, plus one classic answer when a topic calls the flow or one agent action under generative orchestration. Testing in the designer or the agent's test chat uses no capacity.
  • Format limits: desktop flows can't be called; agent flows can't be copied, shared, co-owned or given run-only permissions in Copilot Studio; the Flows page lists only agent flows created there. Express mode is Preview.
Exam traps
  • For a tool, Asynchronous response must be Off.
  • Only the response to the agent is limited to 100 seconds; the run can continue for up to 30 days.
  • Conversion is one-way and needs a solution plus Copilot Studio capacity.
  • A flow missing from the tool list usually lacks the agent trigger or response, has async on, isn't in a solution, or isn't published.

Create a human-in-the-loop agent flow

NeedUse
Pause, collect typed data from named people, reuse it laterRequest for information (Insert a new action → Human review)
Simple sign-off: Approve/Reject or custom responsesStandard approval: Approvals connector, Start and wait for an approval
Staged sign-off mixing people, AI and conditionsRun a multistage approval Preview (Human review connector)
An AI step that should escalate when it is unsureRun an agent with Request human assistance when unsure (emails the connection owner)

Request for information (RFI)

  • Required fields: Title (the email subject), Message and Assigned to (email addresses). With several assignees the first response is used; later ones aren't processed.
  • Requests go out through Outlook only and can't be sent to users outside your tenant.
  • Five input types: Text, Yes/No, Email, Number, Date, with single-select, multi-select and required options. Each input becomes a parameter you can use in later actions.
  1. Flows → New agent flow → add a trigger.
  2. Insert a new action → Human review → Request for information.
  3. Fill Title, Message and Assigned to; Add an input for each value you need.
  4. Use the input parameters in later actions; Save, Publish, Test. The flow pauses until the reviewer answers.
  • Standard approvals (Standard connector, need a Dataverse database): Create an approval (doesn't wait), Start and wait for an approval, Wait for an approval. Types: Approve/Reject with Everyone must approve or First to respond, Custom responses (wait for all or for one), and sequential.
  • Multistage approvals Preview: manual stages (First to respond or Everyone must approve), AI stages (instructions plus inputs; the model returns Approve or Reject with a rationale) and conditions between stages. An AI stage needs Copilot Credits or it stalls; keep a human stage for sensitive or high-value decisions; the same approver can't appear in two stages.
  • Long waits: a tool call must respond within 100 seconds and a run can last up to 30 days, so put the human step after Respond to the agent instead of waiting inline.
Exam traps
  • A standard approval returns a decision (or a custom response); only Request for information collects typed values such as numbers and dates.
  • RFI: first response wins, Outlook only, nobody outside the tenant.
  • Multistage and AI approvals are Preview; AI stages consume Copilot Credits and stall without them.
  • The agent node's “Request human assistance when unsure” emails the connection owner, not a reviewer list.
  • Waiting for a person inside the 100-second tool window ends in a timeout.

Configure actions and connectors

Connectors are proxies around APIs. In an agent they are tools (agent level: Tools → Add a tool → Connector; in a topic: Add node → Add a tool), in an agent flow they are actions, and in knowledge they ground answers. Agent flows are premium flows: standard, premium and custom connectors all work, as long as the plan includes premium connectors.

  1. Agents → select the agent → Tools → Add a tool → Connector → pick the service and the tool.
  2. Create new connection if needed → Submit or Create → Add and configure.
  3. Set description, inputs and authentication, then Save. Custom connector: Add a tool → New tool → Custom connector (opens Power Apps); share the connection from make.powerapps.com → Connections → Share → Can use + share.
SituationDo
Call a SaaS API as the signed-in userTool Authentication = End user (default); users see a Connect card until they connect
Shared service accountMaker-provided credentials: use an authenticated channel; tool Overview → Details → Additional details → Credentials to use; publish and test. An admin can disable this option.
Flow action must use a specific identitySolution flows bind connectors through connection references; update the reference
Error FlowMakerConnectionBlockedAdmin blocked maker credentials: open the flow in Power Automate and share it with run-only permissions
Customer-managed-key environmentUser credentials for flows aren't supported yet; set run-only to specific connections
  • Tool details: Allow agent to decide dynamically when to use the tool (selected by default with generative orchestration), Ask the end user before running (default No), Authentication and a user-facing description.
  • Data policies act at design time (a maker can't save a flow that uses a blocked connector) and at run time (violating flows are suspended). Connectors that exchange data must be in the same data group; premium connectors are allowed in agent flows.
  • Agent node versus prompt node: Run an agent supports full tool orchestration (MCP and connectors), all knowledge sources, human review and multi-turn work; Run a prompt is single-turn, with code interpreter and Dataverse knowledge only and no human review.
Exam traps
  • Default tool credentials are the user's; maker-provided credentials need an authenticated channel and can be switched off by the admin.
  • A custom connector that isn't shared can't be used by other makers' agents.
  • Desktop flows can't be called from agent flows.
  • A blocked connector in the data policy stops the save in the designer, so republishing won't help; the admin must change the policy or group.

Monitor agent flows

WhereUse it to
Overview tabSee name, description, connections, owner and recent runs; turn the flow off or delete it; set up savings (solution-based flows)
Activity tabRun history, status and duration; step through a run to find the failing step; select several runs to resubmit them or cancel those in progress
Analytics tabNumber of runs, failure rate and performance trends
Power Platform admin center → Licensing → Copilot StudioCapacity: the Agent flow actions line per environment; per-agent caps under Manage Agents
  • Analytics limits: runs can take up to 30 minutes to appear; metrics exist only for solution flows; runs of co-owned or shared flows are left out of the Runs count, Run error rate and Flow runs trend; the Actions performed trend refreshes about every 24 hours; totals can differ from the Activity tab.
  • Savings (solution-based flows only): Flows → select the flow → Overview → Savings → set a time-saving rule (a money rule uses an hourly rate or a baseline) → Save. Savings come from successful, non-test runs and can take up to an hour to appear.
  • Capacity enforcement: when prepaid capacity is used up, new agent flow runs are blocked and runs in progress finish; the agent itself keeps working. Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed users and test runs are not affected. Fix it by reallocating capacity, buying credits or turning on pay-as-you-go.
  • Power Automate cloud flows that you didn't convert are monitored in Power Automate, not on the Copilot Studio Flows page.
Exam traps
  • Analytics covers solution flows only and omits co-owned or shared runs, so its totals can be lower than Activity.
  • Test runs produce no savings and consume no capacity.
  • Exhausted agent flow capacity blocks new runs; it does not stop runs already in progress or disable the agent.
  • To see who consumed credits, use the admin center Licensing page; to see why a run failed, use Activity.

Add input and output parameters

  • Add inputs to the When an agent calls the flow trigger and outputs to Respond to the agent. Several Respond actions (for example in different branches) are allowed but must return the same outputs.
  • Types: when a topic invokes the flow, parameters support Text, Boolean and Number (the documented error text); a file travels as a record with contentBytes and name. Human-step inputs differ: RFI = Text, Yes/No, Email, Number, Date; multistage approval = String, Number, Boolean; Run a prompt output = Text, JSON or Document.
  • A parameter's name and description matter: the agent uses them to generate the question when a value is missing.
Input source (tool Inputs, column Fill using)Setting
Value comes from the conversation; ask the user if missingDynamically fill with AI (default)
Fixed value, variable or Power Fx formula; the agent never asksCustom value
Own wording or validationCustomize: display name and description, Identify as, retry logic (reprompt repeats up to 2 times by default), input validation (no valid entity defaults to Escalate)
What the agent says after the tool runsCompletion → After running: Don't respond (default), Write the response with generative AI, Send specific response, Send an adaptive card

Passing a file

Collect the file with a Question node (Identify = File, Entity recognition → Include file metadata) or with First(System.Activity.Attachments), then pass a record. In a topic, with a Question variable named userReceipt:

{ contentBytes: Topic.userReceipt.Content, name: Topic.userReceipt.Name }

On the Tools page a file input only works with Custom value, never with Dynamically fill with AI:

If(
    IsEmpty(System.Activity.Attachments),
    [],
    [{ contentBytes: First(System.Activity.Attachments).Content, name: First(System.Activity.Attachments).Name }])
  • New flow with parameters: Flows → New flow → Agent flow (starter template with trigger and response) → add inputs to the trigger → add the actions → add outputs to Respond to the agent → Publish → add it to the agent as a tool and set Inputs and Completion.
  • Schema drift: after you add, remove or rename an input or output, refresh the flow's inputs and outputs in the agent; if that fails, remove and re-add the flow (BindingKeyNotFoundError).
Exam traps
  • Files need Custom value with a Power Fx record; AI fill can't pass them.
  • Declared type versus evaluated type: a parameter that isn't Text, Boolean or Number, or a null value, ends in FlowActionBadRequest.
  • Respond actions in different branches that return different outputs break the contract with the agent.
  • Editing a published flow's parameters without refreshing the agent causes BindingKeyNotFoundError.

Implement error handling in agent flows

The agent flow docs state that the developer must design an error-handling pattern so the agent knows how to handle exceptions. The building blocks below come from Power Automate's error-handling guidance.

Building blockWhat it does
Run afterRuns an action depending on the previous action's outcome: succeeded (the default), failed, skipped or timed out
Scope (Try / Catch)Group the risky actions in a Try scope; a Catch scope whose Run after is set to run when Try fails identifies the error, logs it and notifies
Retry policy (action settings)For transient faults: Default, None, Fixed interval or Exponential interval (preferred); set the initial interval and the maximum retry count
TerminateStops the run on purpose with a status (for example Failed) and a message
workflow(), result()Run details for logging; results of the actions in a scope, which a Filter array action can filter to find the error

In the stored definition, Run after is the runAfter property. By default an action runs only after Succeeded; this Catch scope runs when Try fails or times out:

"runAfter": {
  "Try": ["Failed", "TimedOut"]
}
Error codeMeaningFix
FlowActionTimedOutMore than 100 seconds to returnOptimize queries and returned data; move actions that can wait after Respond to the agent
FlowActionBadRequestMalformed request: unsupported or mismatched parameter type, missing parameterCheck the base types of the variables you pass (Text, Boolean, Number)
FlowActionExceptionNo output received, or an output parameter is missingCheck the flow for errors; return every output on every path
BindingKeyNotFoundErrorInputs or outputs added, removed or renamedRefresh; remove and re-add the flow
FlowMakerConnectionBlockedAdmin disallows maker credentialsShare the flow with run-only permissions in Power Automate
ExecutionTimeoutA tool or flow action exceeded its timeoutSplit large workflows, optimize queries, remove unnecessary actions from the critical path
  • When an action fails, its successors are marked Skipped, so a Catch scope must change its Run after setting to react.
  • Log error details to a SharePoint list or other store and notify the owner, but avoid excessive custom logging, which hurts performance. Flow checker errors block publishing; warnings don't. Express mode Preview doesn't allow delay or webhook actions.
Exam traps
  • The default Run after is is successful only; a Catch scope never fires until you change it.
  • Retry policies fix transient faults (timeouts, throttling, 5xx), not logic errors. Run after reacts to a failure; Terminate causes one.
  • The 100-second limit applies to the response to the agent, not to the whole run.
  • A scope reports one Failed status; open it to find the failing step.

Sources: Agent flows overview · Create an agent flow as a tool · Agent flow FAQ · Natural language flows · Request for information · Multistage approvals · Standard approvals · Run an agent node · Connectors as tools · Add tools to an agent · Monitor agent flows · Copilot Credits and enforcement · Pass files to connectors · Error handling in Power Automate · Run after and retry policies · Agent error codes

sections.title: 1.3 Configure topics
sections.html:
Skills measured: Add agent flows to a topic • Configure agent response formatting • Add tools to a topic • Configure advanced agent responses with custom prompts • Configure advanced agent responses with custom knowledge sources • Configure advanced agent responses with API and Send HTTP requests • Configure generative answers node • Configure adaptive cards • Manage variables. Build one topic that asks with an Adaptive Card, calls an agent flow and an HTTP request, grounds an answer with a generative answers node, and hands values to a second topic.

Which experience?Topics, nodes, Adaptive Card nodes, variables and agent flows belong to the standard harness (the "classic" experience; reach it from the home page ... menu > Open classic experience). Every Learn page used here carries the note "features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness". Building and monitoring the flows themselves is §1.2; connectors, MCP and REST tools are §2.2.

Add agent flows to a topic

An agent flow GA is a deterministic, rule-based automation built in Copilot Studio. A conversation uses it as a tool: at agent level (the orchestrator can pick it from its description) or at topic level (only that topic can call it, at the exact node you place).

Requirement for a flow used as a toolDetail
TriggerWhen an agent calls the flow (Copilot connector)
ResponseRespond to the agent returns the outputs; if it appears on several branches it must return the same outputs on each
TimingReal-time reply: Asynchronous response Off (Respond to the agent > Settings, under Networking). The eligibility pages quote a 100-second action limit, the async and express-mode pages a two-minute window; design for the shorter one
State and placePublished, and stored in a solution in the same environment as the agent
  1. Create the flow from the Flows page (New flow > Agent flow; the agent-flows overview describes New agent flow on the Workflows page, so the menu path differs by page). The starter template already holds the trigger and the response action; add input parameters to the trigger and output parameters to Respond to the agent.
  2. Add the actions in between, clear every Flow checker error and Publish (a flow with errors can't be published).
  3. Topic level: Topics > open the topic > Add node (+) > Add a tool > pick the flow (the Basic tools tab lists it). An Action node appears.
  4. Map each flow input to a topic, global or system variable (for example System.User.DisplayName) or a literal. The outputs become variables for the later nodes.
  5. Save and test in the test chat. Agent level instead: agent > Tools > Add a tool > Flow > select > Add and configure > set Name, Description, Inputs, Completion > Save.

Existing Power Automate flow: keep it in a solution in the agent's environment, delete its trigger, add When an agent calls the flow and Respond to the agent, then save and publish. To bill it through Copilot Studio, convert it (Edit > change the plan to Copilot Studio > Save); conversion is one-way and needs Copilot Studio capacity.

Agent flow factsDetail
CostFrom a topic: one classic answer (1 Copilot Credit) plus the flow's actions. Under generative orchestration an autonomous action replaces the classic answer. Flow actions cost 13 Copilot Credits per 100 actions. Designer and test-chat runs are free
Capacity emptyNew runs are blocked; runs in progress finish. The no-charge benefit for Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed users covers only runs started through the When an agent calls the flow trigger
Not allowedCan't be copied, shared, co-owned or given run-only permissions; can't call desktop flows. Premium connectors are allowed and no Power Automate license is needed
Long workPut slow actions after Respond to the agent (up to the 30-day run limit). Opt-in asynchronous responses (new-infrastructure environments) let a flow call back later; callbacks work in Teams, not in Microsoft Copilot or telephony channels. Express mode (its Learn page is titled "preview") speeds logic-heavy flows, not data-heavy or fire-and-forget ones
Exam traps
  • Both halves are required: the When an agent calls the flow trigger and the Respond to the agent action. Swapping only one, or using the generic HTTP trigger and Response, doesn't make the flow selectable.
  • A flow added from a topic is a topic-level tool: other topics and the orchestrator can't use it. Add it at agent level when the orchestrator should choose it.
  • Agent flows are not Power Automate cloud flows: no sharing, copying or co-owners, no desktop flows, billed in Copilot Credits.
  • Learn quotes both 100 seconds and two minutes for the response window; on the exam think "reply quickly, push long work after the response action".
  • Testing from the designer or the test chat consumes no capacity; production runs do.

Configure agent response formatting

Formatting happens at several layers. The Message node toolbar adds basic formatting (bold, italic, bulleted and numbered lists), variables ({x}), message variations (one is picked at random each run), speech overrides, images (URL-hosted), videos (a public MP4 or a YouTube URL), basic cards, Adaptive Cards and quick replies. The Question node has the same capabilities.

GoalUse
Fixed wording plus variables, with varietyMessage node, variables, message variations
Rich layout built from variablesAdaptive Card in Formula mode (see Adaptive Cards below)
Different spoken text on a voice channelSpeech override; SSML tags Audio, Break, Emphasis, Prosody
Verbatim, templated tool resultTool Completion > After running > Send specific response
Natural-language reply from tool outputCompletion Write the response with generative AI (the default Don't respond lets the agent fold the output into its own reply); Send an adaptive card is the fourth choice
Style rules for a generative answerCustom instructions on the generative answers node (up to 8,000 characters; they can set tone, rules and format)
Block external images and linksPower Platform admin center > Security > Threat detection > Showing images and URLs: Block all images and other URLs, Block untrusted images and other URLs or Allow images and URLs, per environment or environment group
  • Quick replies suggest answers; types are Send a message (default), Open URL (must start with https://), Make a call (PhoneNumber:1234567890) and Send a hidden message to the agent. Some channels don't support them or limit how many show. To make the user choose from a list, use a multiple-choice Question node.
  • Several media cards display as a Carousel (default) or a vertical List.
  • With generative orchestration, let topics return outputs rather than send the final message, so the agent writes one contextual reply (return an answered-state output too, to avoid duplicates). Don't tell the model to hide sources or answer "only in JSON": uncited answers are withheld when ungrounded responses are off.
  • "Untrusted" images and URLs are those not coming from agent citations, direct user input or go.microsoft.com; blocked items become plain, unclickable text.
Exam traps
  • Quick replies do not force a choice; a multiple-choice Question node does.
  • An Adaptive Card inside a Message or Question node only displays information. The interactive one is the Ask with Adaptive Card node.
  • Customizing a generated answer turns off the automatic citation rendering in Teams; you must render citations yourself.
  • Image and URL blocking is a tenant/environment admin control, not an agent setting.
  • Speech overrides and SSML matter only on voice-enabled channels.

Add tools to a topic

Topics page > open the topic > Add node (+) > Add a tool > choose from the tabs Basic tools, Connector and Tool > an Action node is added > Save. Tool types that exist for agents: connector (prebuilt or custom), agent flow, prompt (Add a tool > New prompt), REST API, Model Context Protocol and computer use. Azure Bot Service skills and client tools are "tool-like".

Classic orchestrationGenerative orchestration (default for new agents)
How tools runOnly when a topic calls them explicitlyThe orchestrator picks tools from name, description, inputs and context; topics can still call them
InputsYou author Question nodesDynamically filled; the agent can ask generated questions
  • Tool configuration has three sections. Details: Name, Description, Allow agent to decide dynamically when to use the tool (on by default with generative orchestration; off = only a topic can call it), Ask the end user before running (default No) and Authentication (End user by default, or Maker-provided). Inputs: Fill using Dynamically fill with AI (default) or Custom value (literal, variable or Power Fx). Completion: see response formatting.
  • Input settings (always available for tool inputs; for topic inputs only with generative orchestration): custom prompt, How many reprompts (default Repeat up to 2 times), retry prompt, additional entity validation with a Power Fx condition, and No valid entity found (Escalate by default, or set a value, or set empty).
  • Topic-only tools: Create search query rewrites the user input with conversation history into a search string; Custom search returns raw, unsummarized results from chosen sources so you can filter them before answering (input can be Activity.text).
  • Limits and governance: up to 128 tools per agent with generative orchestration (aim for 25-30). A tool blocked by a data policy is greyed out with an information icon; blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks MCP tools. Computer use needs generative orchestration and is added from the agent's Tools page. Deleting a tool is possible only from the agent's own Tools page; the Enabled toggle turns it off without deleting.
- kind: CreateSearchQuery
  userInput: =Topic.SearchQueryInput
  result: Topic.SearchQuery
Exam traps
  • In classic orchestration an agent-level tool never fires on its own; call it from a topic or switch to generative orchestration. The dynamic-use setting and the description matter only to generative orchestration.
  • "Ask the end user before running" is a confirmation prompt, not authentication.
  • Topic input settings (reprompts, validation) need generative orchestration; tool input settings don't.
  • Custom search returns raw results; it does not summarize. Create search query only rewrites the query.
  • Maker-provided tool credentials need an authenticated channel (see §2.2).

Configure advanced agent responses with custom prompts

A prompt (prompt builder) is a single-turn, model-based tool: an instruction plus context. Add it at agent level (Tools > Add a tool > Prompt, or the Tools page > New tool > Prompt, which any agent can reuse), at topic level (Add a tool > New prompt) or as Run a prompt under AI capabilities in an agent flow. Prompts made inside a topic, Power Apps or Power Automate don't appear on the Tools page. Prerequisites: a supported region, Copilot Credits and Dataverse in the environment.

Prompt elementFacts
Inputs (/ or Add content)Text, Image or document, Power Fx. Inputs can't carry instructions. Image or document: PNG, JPG, JPEG, PDF; under 25 MB in total; under 50 pages; 100-second processing; not yet supported for prompts used as agent tools; Word/Excel/PowerPoint need code interpreter
KnowledgeDataverse tables; optional filter attribute and value; the Record retrieval setting controls how many records are retrieved (check the current default and maximum in the prompt settings); anonymous agents can't use Dataverse knowledge
Settings (... > Settings)Temperature 0-1 (default 0; disabled for GPT-5 reasoning), Record retrieval, Include links in the response, Enable code interpreter, Content moderation level Low / Moderate (default) / High (managed models only)
OutputText (default), JSON (auto-detected format or a custom example; use Apply, Test, Save custom; schema not editable; keyed objects only) and Document Preview
LimitsExecution capped at 100 seconds; start with the Basic model and move up only when needed
Text(Now(), Input.'Date Format')
  • Power Fx inputs read prompt inputs with Input.'Your input name'; use any Power Fx function that isn't connector-related.
  • To override the agent's or topic's moderation for a prompt tool, set the tool's Completion > After running to Send specific response (specify below) and use Output.predictionOutput.text as the message.
  • Agent flows include a Run a prompt action under AI capabilities. The exact capabilities of the prompt and agent nodes (knowledge types, MCP, human review) are not documented on the pages checked, so confirm them in the current agent-flows documentation.
  • Prompts consume Copilot Credits in Copilot Studio, not AI Builder credits.
NeedUse
Extract, classify, summarize or draft in one turnPrompt tool (JSON output when later steps need fields)
Grounded Q&A over knowledge sourcesGenerative answers node
Tone and rules for the whole agentAgent instructions
Answer style for one generative answers nodeCustom instructions (prompt modification, 8,000 characters)
Exam traps
  • Three different moderation scales: generative answers and agent use Lowest to Highest (default High); prompts use Low / Moderate / High (default Moderate).
  • Temperature is irrelevant for GPT-5 reasoning (slider disabled).
  • Image or document input works in agent-flow prompts, not (yet) in prompts added as agent tools.
  • "Prompt modification" is the generative answers custom instruction field, not the prompt tool.
  • Changing a JSON example makes the format Custom; unsaved changes are lost.

Configure advanced agent responses with custom knowledge sources

Knowledge can be set at agent level (Overview or Knowledge page > Add knowledge) or in a topic's generative answers node. Sources defined in the node override agent-level sources, which then act only as the fallback. Each source needs a unique name and a detailed description (it guides orchestration).

  • Search only selected sources (per node, default off): off = the node searches all agent sources; on = only the sources you tick, and there is no fallback to agent sources.
  • Custom data: for data outside the supported sources, return JSON from a Power Automate flow or an HTTP request and parse it into a Table. Node > Edit under Data sources > Classic data > Custom data (a JSON array or a variable). Columns: Content (required), ContentLocation (optional citation URL), Title (optional citation title). Only the first three rows are used.
  • Answer only from your variable: turn Search only selected sources on, select no source, set Custom data to the variable, and keep Web search and Allow the AI to use its own general knowledge off.
  • Classic data also hosts Bing Custom Search (a Custom Configuration ID) and Azure OpenAI Preview. Under generative orchestration, custom data can't be agent-level knowledge; embed it in a generative answers node. Learn's pages disagree on whether agent-level Bing Custom Search works under generative orchestration, so don't rely on either reading.
  • Variables in URLs: a public-website or SharePoint source can contain a global string variable picked with {x}, for example https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/{GlobalProductURL}. A dynamic SharePoint URL built with Power Fx needs Classic data.
[
  { Content: "Savings APY is 4.1%", ContentLocation: "https://contoso.example/rates", Title: "Savings rates" },
  { Content: "Checking has no monthly fee", ContentLocation: "https://contoso.example/fees" },
  { Content: "Card limits are reviewed yearly", Title: "Card limits" }
]

LookUp(Topic.ProductTable, Product = Topic.Product, Path)
Source typeClassic orchestrationGenerative orchestration
Public websites4 URLs25 websites
SharePoint4 URLs per node25 URLs
Dataverse2 sources, 15 tables eachUnlimited
Custom data / Bing Custom Search / Azure OpenAI3 / 2 / 5Custom data: embed in a generative answers node
Uploaded filesUnlimitedNot part of the 25-source limit
Exam traps
  • Search only selected sources has no fallback; "generative answers as fallback" (Conversational boosting) is a different, agent-level behavior.
  • Custom data uses three rows at most, and without ContentLocation and Title citations are weaker.
  • The official-source flag works only when generative orchestration is off.
  • Custom search (a topic tool) returns raw results; custom data feeds the generative answers node.

Configure advanced agent responses with API and Send HTTP requests

The Send HTTP request node calls a REST API from a topic: Add node > Advanced > Send HTTP request, then set the URL and the Method (GET, POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE). Headers and body > Edit opens HTTP Request properties.

  • Headers: key/value pairs for tokens, content type and so on. A secret can come from a secret environment variable backed by Azure Key Vault (see Manage variables).
  • Body: No Content (default), JSON Content (or Edit JSON > Formula with a Power Fx object) or Raw content (a Power Fx string).
  • Response data type: From Sample Data > Get schema from sample JSON > paste > Confirm gives a typed variable with IntelliSense; Save user response as picks the variable.
  • Error handling: Raise an error (default: the topic stops and the On Error system topic runs) or Continue on error (store the status code and the error response body, for example Topic.StatusCode and Topic.ErrorResponse, and keep going). The error body is type Any; use a Parse value node to get a record.
  • Request timeout is set in milliseconds; the default is 30 seconds.
  • Data policy: block the HTTP connector to stop publishing agents that make HTTP requests, or keep it and use endpoint filtering (Configure connector > Connector endpoints) to allow or deny specific endpoints. A violation also occurs when the HTTP connector sits in a different data group from the other connectors.
NeedUse
One deterministic call inside a topic, header authentication, no specSend HTTP request node
API with an OpenAPI file that the orchestrator calls by description (one environment)REST API tool Preview (§2.2)
Reuse across Power Apps, Power Automate and Logic Apps; OAuth or on-behalf-ofCustom connector (§2.2)
Multi-step, branching, loops, long-runningAgent flow
Server-managed tool list over a standard protocolMCP server (§2.2)
Exam traps
  • The timeout unit is milliseconds, and Continue on error is not the default.
  • The error response variable is Any, not a record, until you parse it.
  • The HTTP node has no managed connection or consent card: credentials travel in headers.
  • Blocking the HTTP connector blocks every HTTP node; endpoint filtering is the way to allow only some endpoints.
  • HTTP output can feed Custom data in a generative answers node.

Configure generative answers node

Add node > Advanced > Generative answers creates a Create generative answers node; ... > Properties opens its settings. When no topic matches, the Conversational boosting system topic (which contains a generative answers node fed by all agent-level knowledge) answers; if that fails, the Fallback system topic runs. With generative orchestration the agent does not use Conversational boosting for knowledge search.

PropertyWhat it does
InputUsually the Activity.Text system variable (the latest user message)
Knowledge sourcesSearch only selected sources, Add knowledge; Web search and Allow the AI to use its own general knowledge toggles
Classic dataBing Custom Search, Azure OpenAI Preview, Custom data
Content moderationLowest to Highest, default High; the lowest level returns the most answers but may allow harmful content. The node (topic) setting wins over the agent's Generative AI setting
AdvancedSend a message (on by default), plus saving the answer to a variable

Customize the answer (documented order):

  1. Set Input to Activity.Text.
  2. Properties > Advanced: create a global variable for the answer and clear Send a message.
  3. Add a Message or Question node and add an Adaptive Card to it.
  4. In the card properties switch to Formula and build the card from the variable.
  • Allow ungrounded responses (agent Generative AI setting, needs generative orchestration): when off, a turn that used no knowledge source or tool is blocked and the Fallback topic runs, and a knowledge answer is returned only with an in-text citation. Add citation instructions rather than suppressing sources.
  • Calls run on behalf of the user. SharePoint content must be modern pages, DOCX, PPTX or PDF; manual authentication needs delegated Graph permissions Files.Read.All and Sites.Read.All.
  • Billing: a generative answer costs 2 Copilot Credits, a classic answer 1. Citations returned from a knowledge source can't be used as inputs to other tools.
Exam traps
  • Node-level moderation overrides the agent setting; if the node isn't set it inherits the agent setting.
  • The lowest moderation level generates more answers, not safer ones.
  • Under generative orchestration, editing the Conversational boosting topic doesn't change how knowledge is searched.
  • Clearing Send a message means you must show the answer, and in Teams you must render the citations.
  • A turn blocked by Allow ungrounded responses = off triggers Fallback, even if the answer came from earlier chat history.

Configure adaptive cards

Adaptive Cards are platform-agnostic JSON UI snippets. Copilot Studio supports schema 1.6 and earlier, but the host decides: Web Chat supports 1.6 without Action.Execute; the live chat widget (Omnichannel for Customer Service) and Teams are limited to 1.5; the test chat renders 1.6 and the authoring canvas doesn't.

Ask with Adaptive Card nodeCard in a Message or Question node
PurposeInteractive: collect inputDisplay only
NeedsAt least one submit buttonNothing interactive
VariablesOutput variables created automatically from the card inputs; fix with Edit SchemaNone
  • Author: Add node > Ask with Adaptive Card > ... > Properties > Edit adaptive card (designer or Card payload editor JSON) > Save. In a Message node: Add > Adaptive card.
  • Behavior: How many reprompts (default Repeat up to 2 times, or once, or not at all), Retry prompt, Allow switching to another topic (default on). Typing text instead of submitting counts as invalid unless it interrupts.
  • Formula mode turns the JSON into a Power Fx record so you can use variables, for example text: Topic.Title. It is one-way: you can't return to the JSON editor, so keep a copy.
  • Each Action.Submit should carry a unique id in data so a click on an older card can be told apart from the current one.
  • Accessibility: always set label on inputs (screen readers read labels, not placeholders), use isRequired with errorMessage, "style": "heading" on headings, and order the JSON as you want the tab order.
{ "type": "Action.Submit", "title": "Confirm",
  "data": { "actionSubmitId": "booking_confirm_card_v3_confirm" } }

{ '$schema': "http://adaptivecards.microsoft.com/schemas/adaptive-card.json", type: "AdaptiveCard", version: "1.5",
  body: [ { type: "TextBlock", text: Topic.Title, weight: "Bolder", wrap: true } ],
  actions: [ { type: "Action.Submit", title: "Submit" } ] }
Exam traps
  • A card that works in the test chat (1.6) can fail in Teams or the live chat widget (1.5).
  • An interactive card without a submit button is invalid; use a Message node for display-only cards.
  • Formula mode is irreversible.
  • Consecutive cards keep their Submit buttons clickable; without a unique submit id the wrong branch can run.
  • Web Chat doesn't support Action.Execute.

Manage variables

ScopeFactsPower Fx prefix
TopicDefault; only the creating topicTopic.
GlobalAny topic; lasts for the session; name unique across topics; can't be turned back into a topic variableGlobal.
SystemCreated by the agent (some hidden), for example Activity.Text, Conversation.Id, User.DisplayName, User.Id, User.LanguageSystem.
EnvironmentCreated in Power Platform; read-only in Copilot Studio; republish after a change, except secret variables (read at runtime)Environment.
  • Types: String, Boolean, Number, Table, Record, DateTime, Choice, Blank. The type is fixed at the first assignment; until then it shows unknown.
  • Set: a Question node creates its variable automatically; Variable management > Set a variable value assigns a literal, a variable or a Power Fx formula (needed for Table and Record). Parse value converts a JSON string into a Record from sample data. Clear variable values resets variables (and can clear the session's conversation history).
  • Global: Variable properties > Global (any topic can access). The Reset Conversation system topic clears globals but, by default, not the conversation history. Deleting a global leaves Unknown references.
  • Pass between topics: set the destination variable to Receive values from other topics; in the source topic add a Redirect node, Add input, pick the destination variable and the value. Return values to original topics sends a value back. Prefer this to globals.
  • Set a global from outside: a dedicated topic with Set variable value nodes; variable named exactly like the external one; Usage Global + External sources can set values; Reference menu Get value from this node if empty; optional timeout in milliseconds (10,000 for Omnichannel); the in-agent value wins. Web: ?UserName=Ana (name without Global.); custom canvas: the pvaSetContext event.
  • Secrets: a secret environment variable reads Azure Key Vault; grant Key Vault Secrets User to the Microsoft Copilot Studio Service app and tag the secret AllowedEnvironments or AllowedAgents ({envId}/{schemaName}). Anyone who can edit the agent could display the value in a message.
  • Topic inputs and outputs: Topic details > Inputs/Outputs, each with name, type and description; with generative orchestration How will the agent fill this input? defaults to Dynamically fill with the best option.
"Welcome, " & System.User.DisplayName
Upper(Text(Topic.customerName))
Topic.bookingDate > DateAdd(Now(), 14)
Exam traps
  • The prefix is Environment. (not Env.), and system variables need System. in formulas.
  • Global-to-topic conversion isn't possible; Reset Conversation doesn't wipe conversation history.
  • Environment variables are read-only in Copilot Studio; editing them needs Power Apps, then a republish (secrets excepted).
  • A global set from outside must be named exactly like the incoming value; a value set inside the agent overrides the context value.
  • The bot. prefix belongs to the Teams-plan wording; the web app uses Global..

sections.title: 2.1 Connect to enterprise knowledge sources
sections.html:
Skills measured: Connect to Copilot connectors • Connect to Microsoft Power Platform connectors • Connect to Azure AI Search. Add one source of each kind to a test agent, ask all three the same question and compare citations, freshness and what each user is allowed to see.

Connect to Copilot connectors

Copilot connectors GA (formerly Microsoft Graph connectors) index an organization's external, non-Microsoft data into Microsoft Graph and respect source-level permissions (ACLs). The content is semantically indexed, so it can ground any Copilot Studio agent, Microsoft Search and Microsoft 365 Copilot, with citations.

WhoWhat they do
Tenant admin (needs the AI administrator role)Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Gallery > choose the source (for example ServiceNow Knowledge or Salesforce) > name, URL, authentication > deploy to a subset of users first > Create; indexing starts. Custom setup tabs: Users (only users with access, or everyone), Content (searchable/queryable/refinable properties, semantic labels such as title and url), Sync
Agent makerAgent > Add knowledge (Overview or Knowledge page, or Properties of a generative answers node) > select the Copilot connector > select the connection > Add to agent. If it isn't listed, open Advanced; if it's still missing, ask the admin
  • Authentication: answers are limited to what the signed-in user may see. For an agent published to channels with manual authentication, include the ExternalItem.Read.All scope. (Sites.Read.All and Files.Read.All are the SharePoint scopes, not these.)
  • Quality and cost: a Microsoft 365 Copilot license in the same tenant plus tenant graph grounding with semantic search gives better results; that grounding adds 10 Copilot Credits per message. Content use is covered by Microsoft 365/Copilot licensing, and an indexing quota applies.
  • Limits: the "enterprise data using connectors" source allows unlimited sources in generative mode and two per agent in classic mode. The source's name and description aren't editable.
Copilot connectorsPower Platform connectors as knowledge Preview
ModelIndex and copy into Graph (semantic index)Real-time, no data movement
Set up byAdmin, Microsoft 365 admin centerMaker or admin, Power Platform connections
Best forDocuments, KBs, tickets, wikis; semantic ranking and citations; reuse in Microsoft Search and CopilotLive facts such as a ticket's current status; no replication; actions are done with tools
LatencyLow (served from the Graph index)Depends on the target API
GovernanceAdmin configuration, indexing quota, Microsoft 365/Copilot licensingPower Platform data policies; standard or premium connectors
Exam traps
  • Copilot connectors are not real-time: content is copied and indexed. "Graph connectors" is the old name.
  • A connector missing from Add knowledge usually means the admin hasn't deployed it; look under Advanced before escalating.
  • The scope for this source is ExternalItem.Read.All; the SharePoint scopes don't help.
  • Pick Copilot connectors for broad, searchable, cited content; pick Power Platform connectors when the data must not be replicated or must be current to the second.
  • Two enterprise-connector sources is the classic-orchestration cap.

Connect to Microsoft Power Platform connectors

Power Platform connectors can ground an agent in two ways. Real-time knowledge Preview: Microsoft indexes only metadata (table and column names); there is no data movement. Each question runs against the source at runtime with the signed-in user's token, so source access controls still apply, and the same Power Platform connections and data policies govern it. Unstructured knowledge bases (Your connections) GA: content is copied, chunked and vector-indexed in Dataverse.

Real-time knowledge PreviewUnstructured knowledge base
ConnectorsSalesforce, ServiceNow, Azure SQL, Azure AI Search, SharePoint, Dataverse, Dynamics 365, Snowflake, Databricks, Zendesk, Confluence (Cloud only), Oracle Database, SAP OData, Google SheetsConfluence (cloud), Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk
Unit addedTablesThe knowledge base or space (not single articles); published articles only
DataNot copiedStored and indexed in Dataverse; refresh every 4-6 hours, no manual refresh
PermissionsUser's token at runtimeLive per-query permission check; users sign in themselves (the maker's connection is only used to create the source)
  1. Agent > Add knowledge (Overview, Knowledge page or generative answers node properties).
  2. Select the connector (Featured, or Advanced) > Add > Sign in > choose the target and credentials > Next.
  3. Select the tables; name and describe the source (the default name reflects the tables).
  4. Optionally add synonyms and glossary definitions (only ServiceNow and Zendesk support them), then Add to agent.
  5. Wait for the status to change from In progress to Ready, then test.
  • Non-queryable tables aren't offered as tables: ServiceNow Knowledge Article, Zendesk Articles, Salesforce Knowledge Article and Knowledge Article Version. Use the Your connections option (unstructured data) instead.
  • Content moderation for enterprise sources: database retrieval questions pass; requests to modify data, plain text searches, support or how-to questions and unstructured-data questions fail.
  • Limits: 500 knowledge objects per agent; unstructured sources need Dataverse search and a Dataverse security role such as Basic User, and have no ALM support and no synonyms or glossary.
  • Typical errors: connection not found or unauthorized (reconnect), ServiceNow instance hibernating, no tables found, firewall, bad gateway (check Deny Public Network Access), forbidden (permissions).
  • The same connector can be knowledge (read and ground, Preview) or a tool (create or update records, GA); choose by whether the agent must read or act.
Exam traps
  • Real-time connector knowledge is Preview and stores only metadata; nothing is copied to Dataverse.
  • Knowledge Article tables are non-queryable: the fix is Your connections, not a different connector.
  • Asking the agent to update a ticket through knowledge fails moderation; use a connector tool.
  • Synonyms and glossary: only ServiceNow and Zendesk; Confluence is Cloud only.
  • Unstructured sources use each user's own sign-in at runtime, not the maker's credentials.

Connect to Azure AI Search

Use Azure AI Search GA when you already own a search index (large corpora, vector or semantic search, custom citation URLs, private networking). Prepare Azure first: an Azure account, an Azure AI Search service and a vector index. Copilot Studio supports integrated vectorization (use Import and vectorize data so the same embedding model also vectorizes the runtime prompt) and the semantic ranker (enable it in Azure before adding the connection).

  1. Agent > Add knowledge (Overview, Knowledge page or generative answers node properties) > Featured > Azure AI Search.
  2. Create new connection and choose the Authentication type: Access Key, Client Certificate Auth, Service principal (Microsoft Entra ID application) or Microsoft Entra ID Integrated.
  3. Enter the details; for key-based authentication that is the Azure AI Search Endpoint URL and the Azure AI Search Admin Key. Create (a green check confirms) > Next.
  4. Enter the vector index; only one vector index can be added. Add to agent.
  5. Wait for Ready, test, and check the cited files.
  • Always add it through the formal data connection; don't hand-configure an endpoint and key. A faulty connection can stop the dialog from loading, and because data connections are environment-level it can affect every agent. Recovery: reset the agent's external access or recreate the agent, then re-add with Entra ID authentication rather than API keys.
  • Citations: include a field with the real document URL. If the index has metadata_storage_path, Copilot Studio uses it as the citation; only if that field is missing does it use any field that holds a complete URL. Users must be allowed to open what the citation points to.
  • Network and licensing: indexes behind a private endpoint work when Virtual Network support is set up for the Power Platform environment. The connector is a Premium connector in Copilot Studio and isn't available in GCC High, China (21Vianet) or DoD.
"fields": [
  { "name": "chunk_id", "type": "Edm.String", "key": true },
  { "name": "chunk", "type": "Edm.String" },
  { "name": "text_vector", "type": "Collection(Edm.Single)" },
  { "name": "metadata_storage_name", "type": "Edm.String" },
  { "name": "metadata_storage_path", "type": "Edm.String" }   // used as the citation
]
ScenarioSource
Existing vectorized index, custom chunking, private endpointAzure AI Search
Third-party KB or tickets, semantic ranking, Microsoft Search reuseCopilot connector
Current record values without copying dataPower Platform real-time connector Preview
Site pages and documents in SharePointSharePoint knowledge (see §1.3 for generative answers nodes)
Exam traps
  • Only one vector index can be added to the knowledge source.
  • The semantic ranker is configured in Azure AI Search, not in Copilot Studio.
  • Key-based auth takes the admin key (not a query key) plus the endpoint URL; the index name comes on the next step.
  • No URL field in the index = no clickable citations; metadata_storage_path wins when present.
  • Azure AI Search is a premium connector with regional exclusions.
  • Using Azure AI Search with a Foundry project is covered in §2.4.
