sections.title: 2.2 Add tools to agents
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure and monitor computer use for an agent • Configure MCP tools • Add a tool by using an existing custom connector • Add REST APIs to an agent. Build one tool of each kind in a test agent and note which ones need generative orchestration, which can sit in a topic, and which are still Preview.

Configure and monitor computer use for an agent

Computer use GA lets an agent operate a Windows computer (websites and desktop apps) with a virtual mouse and keyboard from natural-language instructions. A Computer-Using Agent (CUA) model loops through perception, reasoning, action. Use it when no API exists, for example a legacy invoice-entry application. It requires generative orchestration and cannot run from a topic; the orchestrator calls it as an agent-level tool.

  1. Agent > Tools > Add tool > New tool > Computer use.
  2. Write the instructions (templates are offered) > Add and configure.
  3. Set Name, Description, Model and Instructions, then the optional settings below > Save.
  4. Test (left pane: reasoning and actions; right pane: machine preview) > Stop testing. If you see "not a part of the planned execution sequence", test from the agent's test chat.
ModelTierStatus
OpenAI Computer-Using AgentStandardGA
Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.5StandardGA
Claude Sonnet 4.6StandardExperimental
Claude Opus 4.6PremiumExperimental

Anthropic models need the admin to allow external models.

Optional settingWhat it does
Credentials to useMaker-provided (default; right for autonomous agents; sharing the agent lets users act with the author's access) or End user credentials (each user needs access to the machine)
Stored credentialsHeld in Power Platform storage or Azure Key Vault; type Website or Desktop app; a login domain can use a wildcard such as *.contoso.com
Access controlAllow-list of websites and apps. It blocks actions on sites that aren't listed; it does not block opening them
Enforce HTTPSRefuses non-secure sites (error CuaWebsiteIsNotSecure)
Human supervisionA reviewer gets an Outlook email or an inline card when confirmation is needed; if nobody answers in time the run stops. With no reviewer the session fails. It is probabilistic, not a fail-safe, so never send passwords or personal data through it
Inputs, Machine, ConnectionDynamic values, the target machine, and the connection used to reach it

Where the agent runs

TargetStatusKey facts
Hosted browserPreviewWindows 365 for Agents; no setup; Edge plus built-in Windows apps; Microsoft-managed; not for production; one active session per user; 3-hour maximum session
Cloud PC poolPreviewWindows 365 for Agents; auto-scaling; Entra-joined and Intune-enrolled; up to 2 pools free without a billing plan; 50 free hours per tenant for published autonomous agents; provisioning can take up to 30 minutes; share as Co-owner or User
Your own machineGAPower Automate for desktop 2.61.132.25266 or later (with its web extension), registered to the environment; custom apps and your own controls; runs go through the machine queue

Own-machine setup, in order: install Power Automate for desktop (select the machine-runtime option) > open the machine runtime and sign in > register the machine to the environment > in Power Automate open Machines > the machine > Settings > turn on Enable for computer use > Save > in Copilot Studio add the computer use tool and select the machine > Test.

Billing: the agent-action meter charges 5 Copilot Credits per step, or 15 with a premium model; it isn't covered by the Microsoft Copilot user subscription license.

Monitor and administer

  • Run history: agent > Activity > select a run > Activity map (the steps) or Transcript (reasoning plus screenshots). The side panel adds Session replay, Summary, Websites & applications, Credentials used and Export session logs.
  • Advanced logging lives in the Power Platform admin center: Manage > Environments > the environment > Settings > Products > Features.
SettingValue
Store logs in DataverseOn by default; if turned off, only the default activity logs appear. It also needs the Copilot Studio setting that lets transcripts and metadata be saved in Dataverse
Log verbosityAll data (default: the complete advanced logs), Data without screenshots (the same, minus screenshots), or Minimal (currently behaves like Data without screenshots, and may change)
Log retention timeDefault 7 days (10,080 minutes); the maximum is 33,554,432 minutes; 0 or -1 keeps logs forever
Send audit logs to Microsoft PurviewOptional and independent of the other settings; the activity appears as CUAOperation
StorageDataverse tables flowsession, flowsessionbinary, flowlog consume database, log and file capacity

To turn computer use off for one environment use the same Features page, or the Power Platform CLI; the option then appears greyed out in Add tool. A tenant switch, Manage > Tenant settings > Hosted browser in computer use, controls the hosted browser.

pac auth create
pac env update-settings --environment <envid> --name iscomputeruseinmcsenabled --value false
  • Unsupported: hosted machine groups, multi-screen desktops, running from a topic, and customer-managed keys with the OpenAI CUA model.
  • Errors to recognize: CuaWebsiteIsNotAllowlisted, CuaDesktopAppIsNotAllowlisted, FeatureDisabled, NoCandidateMachine.
  • A standalone computer use tool Preview (Tools > New tool > Computer use) lists runs from the last 28 days; added to an agent it is copied, added to an agent flow as Run a computer use tool it is referenced (latest published version).
  • Hardening: dedicated machine, least privilege, an allow-list, and protection against prompt injection.
Exam traps
  • Computer use itself is GA; the hosted browser, Cloud PC pool and standalone tool are Preview; Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 are Experimental.
  • Access control stops actions, not navigation. Human supervision is not a guarantee.
  • Keeping logs for audits means Store logs in Dataverse plus a longer Log retention time (the default is only 7 days); Purview is a separate, optional switch.
  • These advanced log settings don't change how agent transcripts are stored. Data without screenshots is the level that drops screenshots; All data is the default.
  • A topic can't start computer use; classic orchestration can't use it at all.

Configure MCP tools

Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers publish tools (callable functions), resources (file-like data) and prompts (templates). Copilot Studio supports tools and resources, not prompts, and needs generative orchestration. Names, descriptions, inputs and outputs flow in dynamically from the server, so a server change reaches the agent without edits. Only the Streamable transport is supported; SSE was dropped after August 2025.

Wizard (recommended): agent > Tools > Add a tool > New tool > Model Context Protocol > enter Server name, Server description (it guides the orchestrator) and Server URL > pick the authentication > Create > for OAuth copy the callback URL into the identity provider's app registration > create or pick a connection > Add to agent.

AuthenticationUse whenYou provide
NoneOpen serverNothing
API keySimple shared secretType (Header or Query) and the header or parameter name
OAuth 2.0 > Dynamic discoveryServer supports dynamic client registration (DCR) and discoveryNothing else; simplest
OAuth 2.0 > DynamicDCR but no discovery endpointAuthorization URL and Token URL template
OAuth 2.0 > ManualFixed client registrationClient ID, Client secret, Authorization URL, Token URL template, Refresh URL, optional Scopes

Custom connector route: Tools > Add a tool > New tool > Custom connector > New custom connector > import an OpenAPI file (Swagger 2.0 YAML). The path posts to /mcp, and the operation carries the protocol marker:

swagger: '2.0'
info:
  title: Contoso
  description: MCP Test Specification
  version: 1.0.0
host: contoso.com
basePath: /
schemes:
  - https
paths:
  /mcp:
    post:
      summary: Contoso Lead Management Server
      x-ms-agentic-protocol: mcp-streamable-1.0
      operationId: InvokeMCP
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Success
  • Curate tools: after adding, the configuration page shows Details, Tools and Resources. The Allow all toggle is on by default; turn it off to enable tools one by one, and new server tools then default to off. A resource is usable only when a tool returns it as an output.
  • Governance: MCP access rides on Power Platform connectors, so a data policy that blocks the connector also blocks its MCP tools. An agent can hold at most 128 tools.
  • Known issues: an exclusiveMinimum integer throws a System.FormatException; array-of-types schemas get truncated (use one type); tools with reference-type inputs are filtered out; enum inputs are treated as strings.
  • Building your own server: use the MCP SDKs and choose none, API key or OAuth 2.0; for OAuth register the Copilot Studio callback URL.
Exam traps
  • SSE servers fail; Streamable is the only transport. Prompts from the server aren't surfaced.
  • Discovery available = Dynamic discovery; DCR but no discovery = Dynamic; pre-registered app = Manual.
  • With Allow all off, tools added to the server later start disabled.
  • A data policy that blocks the connector also blocks the MCP tools behind it; classic orchestration can't use MCP.
  • Prefer the wizard; the custom connector route is for customizing the OpenAPI definition.

Add a tool by using an existing custom connector

Custom connectors made in the Power Apps maker portal appear in the same connector gallery as prebuilt ones. Adding one is the same flow: agent > Tools > Add a tool > Connector > pick the connector > pick the operation > create or select a connection > Add and configure > set Name, Description and Inputs. At topic level use Add node > Add a tool > Connector (see §1.3). The New tool > Custom connector command, by contrast, creates a connector in Power Apps.

TopicFacts to know
Sharing the connectormake.powerapps.com > Data > Custom connectors > the connector > Invite another user > Can view or Can edit > Save
Sharing a connectionmake.powerapps.com > Connections > Share > Can use + share
Credentials to useDefault is the end user. Maker-provided uses one identity for everybody and requires an authenticated channel; set it under Details > Additional details > Credentials to use
OrchestrationTool inputs default to Dynamically fill with AI; the Name and Description are what the orchestrator reads to choose the tool. Agent-level tools are model-selected; topic-level tools are deterministic
LimitsConnector payload 5 MB (GCC 450 KB). A data policy can block custom connectors. SSO isn't supported for custom Active Directory authentication in Teams

On-behalf-of (OBO) with Microsoft Entra ID, so calls run as the signed-in user:

  1. Optionally register a service app and expose a scope for your custom API or MCP server.
  2. Register the connector app with delegated permissions, grant admin consent, create a client secret, and under Expose an API authorize the Azure API Connections service principal (fe053c5f-3692-4f14-aef2-ee34fc081cae).
  3. On the connector's Security tab choose OAuth 2.0 with Microsoft Entra ID and set Enable on-behalf-of login to true.
  4. Copy the connector's Redirect URL into the app registration (Web platform), then share the connector (Can edit for collaborating makers, Can view for end users).
  5. Users get a consent prompt on first use.
Exam traps
  • Maker-provided credentials need an authenticated channel: configure the channel first, then set Credentials to use.
  • A connector that a collaborating maker can't see was probably never shared from Power Apps.
  • Connector sharing (Can view/Can edit) and connection sharing (Can use + share) are different dialogs.
  • Custom connectors are reusable in Power Apps, Power Automate and Logic Apps; they also carry OAuth and OBO.

Add REST APIs to an agent

The REST API tool Preview turns an OpenAPI description into agent tools without building a connector first. You need maker credentials and a Copilot Studio license; supply the OpenAPI v2 (Swagger) JSON file, the authentication details and good descriptions. An OpenAPI v3 file is translated to v2 automatically. The tool description is pre-filled from the spec's info object.

  1. Agent > Tools > Add a tool > New tool > REST API.
  2. Upload the spec, write the description, choose a solution (blank = the system creates one with the default publisher) > Next.
  3. Authentication: None; API key (Parameter label, Parameter name, Parameter location = Header or Query; the user supplies the key at first use); or OAuth 2.0 (Client ID, Client secret, Authorization URL, Token URL, Refresh URL, optional Scope, which Microsoft 365 organization may access it, which app (client) may use it).
  4. Select and configure tools: choose endpoint and method pairs, set a Tool name and Tool description; parameter names and types can't change but their descriptions can and must not be blank.
  5. Review and publish, then Create connection and, on Add tool > REST API, pick the tool, select the connection and choose Add and configure.
{
  "swagger": "2.0",
  "info": { "title": "Tickets", "description": "Search and update support tickets", "version": "1.0" },
  "host": "api.contoso.com",
  "paths": { "/tickets": { "get": { "operationId": "ListTickets", "summary": "Get tickets" } } }
}
NeedUse
No connector exists, one environment, spec availableREST API tool Preview
Reuse across Power Apps or Power Automate, OAuth or OBO, certificationCustom connector
One-off call inside one topic with Power Fx controlSend HTTP request node (see §1.3)
Server that publishes its own tools and resourcesMCP
Legacy UI with no APIComputer use
Approvals and multi-step logicAgent flow (see §1.2)
Production-critical todayPrefer GA options (custom connector, HTTP node)
  • Descriptions drive selection: say what the tool does, on which system, with which data, and add synonyms ("get, retrieve, find, display tickets"). Select only the endpoints you need to keep the tool surface small.
  • Reuse: the tool is stored on the environment's Tools page and can be added to other agents in the same environment. Microsoft's docs state that creating the tool also creates a custom connector, so check the current docs before assuming whether it can be used outside Copilot Studio. Keep it in a solution to move it across environments (see §3.2).
  • Data policies and connector rules still apply to the generated tools.
Exam traps
  • It is Preview. The spec format is v2 JSON; v3 is converted, so there is no need to convert by hand.
  • A blank parameter description blocks the wizard; a vague tool description means the orchestrator never calls it.
  • API key placement is Header or Query; the label, name and location are three separate fields.
  • The REST API tool is not an existing custom connector, but it does generate one.

sections.title: 2.3 Configure multi-agent collaboration from Copilot Studio
sections.html:
Skills measured: Design multi-agent solutions in Copilot Studio • Integrate a Foundry agent • Integrate an existing agent in Copilot Studio • Integrate a Fabric data agent • Create a multi-agent solution by using A2A protocol. Build one main agent with a child agent and a connected agent in a test environment, then add a Foundry agent, a Fabric data agent and an A2A agent, and read the activity map after each call.

Design multi-agent solutions in Copilot Studio

This group assumes an agent on the standard harness with generative orchestration. The main agent routes to child and connected agents by their description; under classic orchestration agents are "not applicable". Every agent you add appears on the main agent's Agents page.

OptionWhat it isChoose it when
Child agentLightweight agent inside the main agent with its own instructions, knowledge and tools. It always receives the parent's conversation context.One intent or task, one small team, no separate settings, authentication, publishing or reuse.
Connected agentA separate published Copilot Studio agent in the same environment with its own orchestration, model setting and ALM.Several teams, separate publishing and channels, independent ALM, or reuse by more than one main agent.
External agentAn agent outside Copilot Studio: A2A, Microsoft Foundry, Fabric data agent, Microsoft 365 Agents SDK.The capability already lives on another platform.
  • When to split: routing precision degrades when the main agent has more than 30-40 choices of action (tools, topics, other agents), and sooner when descriptions are similar. Sharpen the descriptions first, then split, and judge with your own evaluations (§3.1). You can mix child and connected agents.
  • Costs: every extra layer adds an orchestration hop (latency) and enlarges the test, management and governance surface.
  • Tool limits: the orchestrator supports up to 128 tools per agent; best results come from 25 to 30. Each child agent has its own orchestration and its own limit.
  • Redirect: a topic can redirect to a child or connected agent (Add node > Add an agent); the originating topic resumes afterwards. Reference an agent in the main agent's instructions by typing / in Overview > Instructions. Manage agents with the Enabled toggle, Delete (child) or Disconnect agent (connected).

Build a child agent (ordered): Agents page > Add > New child agent > distinctive name > choose when it runs (default The agent chooses - Based on description) > instructions (type / for tools, variables, Power Fx) > optional agent-specific knowledge and tools > Save. Other options under When will this be used? include message received, custom client event, an activity occurs, the conversation changes, it's invoked, it's redirected to, the user is inactive, a plan completes, and an AI-generated response is about to be sent. Priority: a lower number runs first; ties run oldest first. To stop the orchestrator calling a tool directly, clear Allow agent to decide dynamically when to use this tool.

Inputs have a display name, description, data type, Make this input required, and advanced prompting (Should prompt user, up to two reprompts, conditions). After running controls what the parent does when the child finishes: Don't respond (default), Write the response with generative AI, Send specific response or Send an adaptive card.

Context ruleDetail
Child agentAlways gets the parent's context; no setting to turn it off.
Connected agentPass conversation history to this agent (on by default); clear it to pass only the explicit task.
Tool or flowReceives only its inputs.
OrchestratorCan't see what a subagent says to the user, which is why duplicate or missed answers happen.

Avoid duplicate messages: treat inputs and outputs as the contract between parent and subagent. A subagent that returns no outputs is a red flag.

NameDirectionMeaning
scopedRequestinput (and output)The exact request the subagent must fulfill; repeat it as an output so the top level can plan multi-intent turns.
answeredoutputTrue when the user already received the answer; set on every subagent.
interactionSummaryoutputSummary of what the subagent told the user (subagent spoke directly).
findingsoutputThe answer for the parent to deliver (subagent stayed silent).
openQuestionsoutputParts of the request left unanswered.
Do NOT reply or communicate with the user directly.
Only fulfill the scopedRequest provided in the input and respond with the result.
  • Telling the parent "you're the only agent that talks to the user" doesn't work: the parent can't stop a running subagent. The subagent must be told to stay silent, and After running doesn't stop its messages. Add one top-level instruction that checks the answered output before the parent replies.
  • Guidance for parents and subagents: declare the subagent role, use directive wording (MUST, NEVER), give each subagent a distinct, non-overlapping knowledge source and a distinct description, define the orchestration pattern in the parent, repeat "no direct reply" in the delegated task, test domain-mismatch questions, and prefer ask over inform when a follow-up is expected.
  • Known limits: a main agent that has connected agents can't also be a connected agent of another main agent; child and connected agents respect the main agent's Use general knowledge setting; citations may be lost on the way back.
  • MCP vs A2A: MCP lets one orchestrator select and control tools; A2A connects peer agents that stay opaque and run their own orchestration. MCP tools and custom connectors are covered in §2.2.
Exam traps
  • "128 tools" is a ceiling; the guidance is 25-30 and splitting starts to pay off around 30-40 choices.
  • Child agents can't be published, versioned or reused on their own; that needs connected agents.
  • Don't respond is the default After running value, and it doesn't silence a subagent.
  • The history checkbox exists only for connected agents; a child agent always gets the parent's context.
  • The guidance page calls child agents "inline agents ... often just topics", but the child agent you create is a full lightweight agent with instructions, knowledge, tools, inputs and outputs.

Integrate a Foundry agent Preview

The Copilot Studio article is titled "Connect to a Microsoft Foundry agent (preview)". The product is now named Microsoft Foundry; older pages and the connector still say Azure AI Foundry.

  • Prerequisite: the Foundry agent must have the Activity protocol endpoint enabled. A new Foundry agent does not have the Activity protocol enabled (Microsoft's pages describe the other protocols inconsistently: Responses is on by default, and one article lists A2A as on by default while the A2A article says it must be enabled with a PATCH call), and calls then fail at runtime with HTTP 400. You can enable Activity only programmatically (REST API or Python SDK), not in the Foundry portal; the portal's Endpoints list keeps showing only Responses and A2A afterwards, which is expected.
  • Only agents created in the new Microsoft Foundry portal work; an agent from the previous portal gives 404 - Version not found.
  • The connection needs the Foundry project endpoint URL. The connector is Azure AI Foundry Agent Service (Preview) with Microsoft Entra ID user login (not shareable), 1000 calls per 60 seconds per connection.
The connector 'Azure AI Foundry Agent Service' returned an HTTP error with code 400.
Inner Error: Agent 'orders-agent' endpoint does not support activity.
Please update the agent endpoint to support this protocol.

Steps (ordered): enable the Activity protocol on the Foundry agent > Agents page > Add an agent > Connect to an external agent > Microsoft Foundry > choose or create the connection (project endpoint URL) > Next > Name and Description > Agent Id > Add Agent > test. The Agent Id can be changed later from the agent's details page. The description tells the orchestrator when to call the agent, so make it specific.

Foundry endpoint topicFacts
ProtocolsResponses, Activity Protocol, Invocations, A2A (v1.0 GA, v0.3 Preview), MCP (Preview)
AuthorizationEntra (caller needs Foundry Agent Consumer or higher), BotServiceRbac, BotServiceTenant; API keys aren't supported
PublishingThe GitHub Copilot harness article adds that publishing a Foundry prompt agent to Microsoft 365 or Teams also enables Activity and BotServiceRbac for you
RolesFoundry User, Owner, Account Owner and Project Manager were renamed from Azure AI User, Owner, Account Owner and Project Manager

Integrate an existing agent in Copilot Studio

To connect a main agent to another Copilot Studio agent: the other agent must be in the same environment, published, configured to allow connections from other agents, and you must own it or have it shared with you. Depending on authentication you may also need to share it with the main agent's end users.

  1. On the main agent's Agents page select Add an agent.
  2. Under Connect to an external agent select Copilot Studio.
  3. Pick the agent (its name, instructions and description appear).
  4. Refine the description so it doesn't overlap with other tools or agents.
  5. Optionally clear Pass conversation history to this agent so only the explicit task is passed.
  • Make an agent connectable: Settings > Let other agents connect to and use this one. By default any agent in the environment can connect; turn the option off to block it.
  • Publish every change to the connected agent; the main agent only uses the latest published version. The description is controlled locally and never syncs, so update it by hand.
  • A Preview sibling is the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK agent: enter its messaging endpoint (by default it ends with /api/messages), a name, a description and the authentication, then add it.
RequirementFailure symptom
Same environmentAgent isn't offered in the list
PublishedMain agent keeps using the older published behavior
Allow other agents to connectAgent can't be added

Integrate a Fabric data agent Preview

A Fabric data agent answers natural-language questions over Fabric data by generating read-only queries (NL2SQL, NL2DAX, NL2KQL). The Fabric feature itself is GA; the Copilot Studio connection is labeled preview.

  1. Confirm the data agent works, and publish it with a detailed description.
  2. In Copilot Studio open the main agent's Agents page > Add an agent > Connect to an external agent > Microsoft Fabric.
  3. Create or select the connection, select Next, pick the data agent and adjust the description.
  4. Under Additional details choose User authentication (users need access to the data agent and its sources) or Agent author authentication.
  5. Make sure generative orchestration is on, test, then publish.
  • Prerequisites: paid F2 or higher capacity (or Power BI Premium P1 or higher) with Fabric enabled; the Fabric tenant settings for Copilot and Azure OpenAI and cross-geo processing and storing; a data source you can read; the data agent and the Copilot Studio agent in the same tenant, signed in with the same account.
  • Limits: no Redirect node and no explicit reference in instructions; the combination doesn't work when the main agent is deployed to Microsoft Copilot (documented as validated only for Teams); agent evaluation (§3.1) doesn't support Fabric data agents.
  • A data agent uses up to five data sources, is read-only, runs with the user's permissions, and its responses may leave Fabric's compliance boundary or region.

Create a multi-agent solution by using A2A protocol

The Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol is an open standard for agents to exchange tasks. Copilot Studio can delegate work to an A2A agent, not just call an API. The docs don't mark the A2A connection as preview (Foundry, Fabric and Microsoft 365 Agents SDK are).

FeatureA2A protocolHTTP connector
Designed for agent workflowsYesNo
Multiturn interactionsYesNo
Rich contextual metadataYesLimited
Interoperable across frameworksYesVaries
  1. Agents page > Add agent > A2A agent.
  2. Enter the agent's endpoint URL (the communication endpoint, not the agent-card URL). If a valid agent card exists on the standard .well-known location, name and description fill in automatically; otherwise type them.
  3. Choose Authentication: None, API key (header or query-parameter name) or OAuth 2.0 (client ID, client secret, authorization URL, token URL, refresh URL).
  4. Save, pick or create the connection, then Add and configure.

A2A connections use the custom connector infrastructure, so agents running on-premises or inside a virtual network can be reached. Each request carries a contextId, message IDs, locale and the full chat history:

{ "method": "message/send",
  "params": { "message": {
    "contextId": "ee1e68ee-75fc-42bb-83d7-25fd26e559c3",
    "metadata": {
      "copilotstudio.microsoft.com/a2a/chathistory": [
        { "From": "user", "Locale": "en-US", "Text": "Which plant needs more sunlight..." } ] } } } }
Integration needUse
Plain APIs or basic HTTP servicesCustom connectors or HTTP tools
MCP tools or resourcesMCP servers
Agent built with the Microsoft 365 Agents SDKThe SDK agent option (Activity Protocol)
Agent that already speaks A2AA2A agent

The documented sample is the Simple-A2A-Sample in the microsoft/CopilotStudioSamples repository (.NET 10 SDK, Azure OpenAI settings, Dev Tunnels for development only). Exposing a Copilot Studio agent as an A2A server is a separate GitHub Copilot harness Preview channel and isn't part of this skill.

Exam traps
  • Foundry needs the Activity protocol; A2A, MCP and Responses on the Foundry agent are not what Copilot Studio's Foundry option calls.
  • Foundry agents from the previous portal fail with 404, not 400; a missing Activity endpoint fails with 400.
  • A2A: paste the message endpoint, not the agent-card address; an empty name and description only means the card wasn't found.
  • Fabric: publish the data agent, use the same tenant and account, and don't plan on Redirect nodes or Microsoft 365 Copilot deployment.
  • Connected-agent descriptions don't sync, and an unpublished change isn't used.
  • Don't confuse the three harnesses: this section describes the standard harness.

sections.title: 2.4 Integrate agents with Azure
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure generative answers by using Azure AI Search with Foundry • Configure custom prompts to use the Foundry model catalog • Monitor agents by using Application Insights. Ground one agent on an Azure AI Search index, add a prompt tool that runs on a Foundry deployment, send telemetry to Application Insights, then query it with Kusto.

Configure generative answers by using Azure AI Search with Foundry

Two routes reach Azure-hosted data. Know which one is current.

RouteHow you add itStatus
Azure AI Search knowledge sourceAdd knowledge > Featured > Azure AI Search, on the agent or in a generative answers nodeNo preview label in the docs
Azure OpenAI on your dataGenerative answers node > Classic data > Azure OpenAI connection; or in Foundry Deploy to > A new Microsoft Copilot Studio botPreview page in Copilot Studio; the Azure service Retired Oct 14, 2026

Add an Azure AI Search knowledge source (ordered):

  1. In Azure AI Search create a vector index that uses integrated vectorization, so the same embedding model vectorizes the user's prompt at run time. To use the semantic ranker, configure it in Azure AI Search first.
  2. In Copilot Studio select Add knowledge (Overview page, Knowledge page, or the node's Properties) > Featured > Azure AI Search.
  3. Select Create new connection, choose the Authentication type, enter the endpoint URL and credentials, then Create and Next.
  4. Type the vector index name and select Add to agent. The status shows In progress, then Ready. Test.
TopicRule
Authentication typesAccess Key, Client Certificate Auth, Service principal (Microsoft Entra ID application), Microsoft Entra ID Integrated
Index countA knowledge source uses only one vector index
Connection styleUse the formal data connection. Hand-typing the endpoint and key can leave a faulty environment-level connection that breaks the dialog; recover with Data sources > Azure AI Search and Entra ID
CitationsNeed a URL field. metadata_storage_path is used when present, otherwise any field holding a full URL; readers still need access to the cited source
NetworkPrivate endpoint plus Power Platform virtual network support
  • Generative answers node: sources chosen in the node override agent-level sources. Search only selected sources replaces the agent-level set and does not fall back to it. Azure OpenAI, Bing Custom Search and Custom data are not offered as knowledge sources there; use the Classic data option.
  • Classic orchestration lets the Conversational boosting topic search up to 5 Azure OpenAI connections.
  • Foundry's role: Foundry hosts the models. The Azure AI Search Import data wizard (Copilot Studio's docs call it "Import and vectorize data") can embed with models from the Foundry model catalog, and the search service's identity then needs the Foundry Project Manager role.
  • Migration: Microsoft's path off Azure OpenAI on your data is Foundry IQ, a knowledge base on Azure AI Search agentic retrieval. The migration is not automatic. The Foundry IQ connection documented in Copilot Studio today is a tool for GitHub Copilot harness agents, not a standard-harness knowledge source.

Configure custom prompts to use the Foundry model catalog

Prompts can run on a model you deployed in Foundry instead of the built-in model. The Foundry model catalog lists more than 1,800 models. The feature works in Copilot Studio, Power Apps and Power Automate. It is a different feature from choosing the agent's primary model (Anthropic, Mistral, xAI), which an admin enables separately.

  1. Open the agent > Tools > Add a tool > New tool > Prompt (topic route: Topics > + > Add a topic > New prompt).
  2. Write the instructions and add input variables.
  3. Open the Model dropdown > + > Connect a model from Azure AI Foundry.
  4. Enter the Model deployment name and the Base model name exactly as Foundry shows them, plus the model endpoint, then Connect.
  5. Select the new model and add the prompt to the agent.
RuleDetail
Model typeChat completion models only; the GPT-5 family and later aren't supported
Endpoint shapeMust end with /chat/completions; a Responses URL returns Resource not found
GovernanceData policy connector named Azure AI Foundry in the Power Platform admin center; each model connection also appears on the Connections page
Safety settingsThe content moderation slider is unavailable for Foundry and Anthropic models; apply responsible-AI controls in Foundry
CostPrompts in Copilot Studio consume Copilot Credits
Other settingsTemperature 0-1 (default 0), Record retrieval, Include links in the response, Enable code interpreter; vision input limits the list to vision-capable models
Valid:   https://{resource}.services.ai.azure.com/openai/deployments/{deployment}/chat/completions
Invalid: https://{resource}.services.ai.azure.com/openai/v1/responses   (Resource not found)

Monitor agents by using Application Insights

Application Insights (Azure Monitor) needs an Azure subscription. There are two scopes with different tables.

AreaAgent-levelEnvironment-level Preview
ConfiguredPer agent, by the makerOnce per environment, by an admin
HarnessStandard harness onlyStandard and GitHub Copilot harness
Data modelEvents in customEvents; the overview lists no OpenTelemetry alignmentSpans in dependencies, aligned with OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions
Best forMessages, topic and node events of one agentInvocations, tool execution and cross-agent traces
PrerequisiteAccess to the agent's configurationManaged environment; tenant-level Power Platform or Dynamics 365 admin plus an administrator role in the Dataverse environment
  • Agent-level setup: Settings > Advanced > Application Insights > paste the Connection string (some text still says instrumentation key). Optional toggles: Enable logging (incoming and outgoing messages and events), Log conversation details (user ID, user name and message text), Log sensitive Activity properties (values of properties that could be sensitive) and Node execution events (an event each time a topic node runs). Query in the Azure Logs blade.
  • Custom dimensions include type, channelId, fromId, fromName, locale, text and designMode, which is True when the conversation happened in the test canvas. The dashboard is under Monitoring > Workbooks > Copilot Studio Dashboard (Preview); sharing it needs Reader on the resource.
  • Block agent-level telemetry: in the Power Platform admin center use Security > Data and privacy > Data policy and block the connector Application Insights in Copilot Studio.
  • Environment-level setup: admin center Manage > Data export > App Insights tab > New data export > data type Copilot Studio > filters, source environment, subscription, resource group and Application Insights resource. Data arrives within 24 hours. Declarative agents are excluded.
  • Spans are InvokeAgent, ExecuteTool and OutputMessages, grouped by operation_Id and nested through operation_ParentId, with gen_ai.* attributes. Get a conversation ID in test chat with /debug conversationid.
customEvents
| extend isDesignMode = customDimensions['designMode']
| where isDesignMode == "False"
dependencies
| where tostring(customDimensions["gen_ai.conversation.id"]) == "{ConversationId}"
| order by operation_Id asc, iff(name == "InvokeAgent", 0, 1) asc, timestamp asc

The first query keeps production traffic and drops design-time test chats. The second lists one conversation's spans with the root InvokeAgent span first.

Exam traps
  • Azure OpenAI on your data is a preview page in Copilot Studio and a retired Azure service; don't choose it for new work.
  • A knowledge source takes only one vector index, and citations need a URL field.
  • Search only selected sources in a node never falls back to agent-level sources.
  • Prompt models must expose a chat completions endpoint; a Responses endpoint fails and GPT-5 family models aren't supported.
  • customEvents means agent-level; dependencies means environment-level, which needs a managed environment and is in preview.
  • The setting asks for a connection string, even where the text says instrumentation key.

sections.title: 3.1 Evaluate agent performance
sections.html:
Skills measured: Create a test set • Choose an evaluation method • Review test results. Generate a test set from your knowledge sources, run it with two methods, edit an instruction, rerun the same set, use Compare with, then export the CSV and start a run through the REST API.

Create a test set

A test case is one interaction, either a question or a whole conversation. A test set is a group of cases you run together. Everything below is the standard harness Evaluation page; the GitHub Copilot harness has its own Evaluate tab (Preview). Open Evaluation > New evaluation and pick the test type. Runs execute as the signed-in user.

Single responseConversation
Cases per setUp to 100Up to 20
Size of a caseOne question and answerUp to 12 messages (6 question and answer pairs)
Use it to testIsolated Q&A, wording, capability checksContext retention, clarifying questions, multi-step tasks
Quick optionQuick question set: 10 questions from the agent's description, instructions and capabilitiesQuick conversation set: 10
Other sourcesFull question set (knowledge sources or topics, you set the count), test chat, import, manual, production themes (Preview)Full conversation set (short or long), test chat
  • Generate from knowledge sources or topics: knowledge sources suit agents on generative orchestration; topics suit classic orchestration. Files used for generation (text, Word, Excel, PDF, or individual SharePoint files, not folders) can be up to 5 MB. Generation fails if the questions would violate content moderation, and it is a poor way to test information gaps.
  • Import a .csv or .txt file. The first-row headings must be Question then Expected response; at most 100 questions, each up to 1,000 characters. A CSV template is under New evaluation > Import. Expected responses are optional at import but the match-based methods need them.
  • After you pick the source: Name > Add test method (set a pass score) > expected responses, keywords or tools as the method requires > Additional configuration > Save or Run. Edit later in bulk, or use Add questions / Add conversations.
  • Not supported: Fabric data agents, and agents whose authentication is Authenticate manually. Supported are No authentication and Authenticate with Microsoft. Any maker with access to the agent sees its test sets, and generated cases can contain sensitive data.
Question,Expected response
How many vacation days do new hires get?,New hires get 15 vacation days per year.
Can unused days carry over?,Up to 5 unused days carry over.

Choose an evaluation method

MethodWhat it checksTest typesNeeds
General qualityLLM judge: relevance, groundedness, completeness, abstention. Default on every setSingle, conversationNo expected answer
Content safetyHate, sexual, violence, self-harm; severity 0 (strictest) to 7BothContent type and level
Compare meaningSame intent and meaning; default pass score 50SingleExpected answer
Tool useExpected tools or topics were usedSingleExpected tools or topics
Keyword matchAny or All of your keywords appearBothKeywords
Text similarityWording closeness by cosine similaritySingleExpected answer
Exact matchCharacter-for-character equalitySingleExpected answer
CustomYour own instructions with at least two labels, each marked pass or failBothName, instructions, labels
If you needUse
No reference answers at allGeneral quality
Different wording is fine if the meaning is rightCompare meaning
Wording must stay near-identical (legal text)Text similarity
A fixed code, number or ID stringExact match
Required terms must appearKeyword match
Proof that a specific tool or topic ranTool use
A domain rule, such as refusals counting as correctCustom
  • A case missing the data a method needs is scored Invalid for that method. You can attach several methods to one set.
  • General quality can mark an appropriate refusal down because of its abstention check; switch to a Custom method for that rule. It can also error when retrieved knowledge makes the grading input too large.
  • Compare meaning fails a response whose language doesn't match. In GCC environments there is no Text similarity method and no user profile.
  • Safety methods don't guarantee safety; keep your responsible-AI review.
Docs disagree on conversation setsBoth articles' method tables list Content safety for single-response and conversation sets and Tool use for single responses only, but the conversation article's step text names General quality, Keyword match, Tools use and Custom. General quality, Keyword match and Custom are consistent everywhere; check the methods the UI offers for the other two.

Review test results

  • Each case ends Pass, Fail, Invalid or Error. Each run gets a Pass rate, listed under Evaluation > Recent results (See all). Filter by All, Pass or Fail.
  • Case detail shows expected versus actual, the reasoning, the knowledge, topics and tools used, the transcript, and Show activity map. The thumbs up or down rates the evaluation method's verdict, not the agent's answer.
  • Only one run at a time. You can stop a run and rerun it with Evaluate.
  • Compare with needs the same test set run at least twice. Arrows mark improved (fail to pass) and declined cases. A different test set isn't comparable.
  • Response time is end-to-end seconds per interaction. It's a measurement, not a pass or fail.
  • Results stay in Copilot Studio for 89 days. Export a CSV (question, expected answer, method, pass score, response, result, analysis) to keep them longer.
  • Everyone sees run status and metrics; only the maker who ran the evaluation sees the responses and explanations. The Agent viewer role can view, run, rename, cancel and delete evaluations but can't create or update test sets or edit the agent.
  • User-authenticated runs need the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector to be allowed by data policy. The Review button warns when no evaluation exists or the model changed, but doesn't block publishing.

Automate with the Power Platform API. You need the environment ID, the bot ID, an existing test set and a Microsoft Entra user access token. A run is asynchronous. The optional mcsConnectionId supplies a user profile; without it the run is unauthenticated.

GET  https://api.powerplatform.com/copilotstudio/environments/{EnvironmentId}/bots/{BotId}/api/makerevaluation/testsets?api-version=2024-10-01
POST https://api.powerplatform.com/copilotstudio/environments/{EnvironmentId}/bots/{BotId}/api/makerevaluation/testsets/{TestSetId}/run?api-version=2024-10-01
GET  https://api.powerplatform.com/copilotstudio/environments/{EnvironmentId}/bots/{BotId}/api/makerevaluation/testruns/{TestRunId}?api-version=2024-10-01

Flow actions mirror these calls: Evaluate Agent, Get Agent Test Run Details, Get Agent Test Runs, Get Agent Test Set Details, Get Agent Test Sets.

Exam traps
  • The limits are 100 single-response cases but only 20 conversation cases of at most 12 messages; a nine-question dependent dialog needs splitting.
  • The create-a-test-set article says every method except general quality requires expected responses or keywords, but its method tables list no expected answer for Content safety or Custom, so the documentation is inconsistent on those two. Match, similarity and compare-meaning methods clearly need expected responses; a method yields Invalid when its required data is missing.
  • Compare meaning tolerates rewording; Text similarity and Exact match don't.
  • Pass rate comes from graded methods; response time is measured but never passes or fails.
  • Compare with needs two runs of the same test set; results vanish after 89 days unless exported.
  • Manual authentication and Fabric data agents can't be evaluated.

Sources: Agent evaluation overview · Create a test set · Conversation test sets · Test methods · Review results · Automate evaluations with the API · Edit test sets

sections.title: 3.2 Implement application lifecycle management (ALM) for agents in Copilot Studio
sections.html:
Skills measured: Create a solution • Add existing agents to a solution • Create and use environment variables • Implement and extend Microsoft Power Platform Pipelines. Build a custom solution with a preferred-solution setting, add an agent and its required objects, export and import it, add a Text and a Secret environment variable, then deploy through a pipeline and extend it with an approval flow.

Create a solution

Agents live in solutions. Anything you build without choosing one lands in the Default Solution, the "carrier" for loose components, which is not a container you can deploy. To move an agent between environments, or to use pipelines, put it in a custom solution.

UnmanagedManaged
WhereDevelopment environments, where you buildTest and production
EditingComponents editable; your source of truth, so check exports into source controlComponents can't be edited directly
ExportExport as unmanaged or managedCan't be exported

A managed solution can't be imported into the environment that holds its originating unmanaged solution, so test it in a separate environment.

  1. Open the solution explorer (sidebar ... > Solutions) > New solution.
  2. Enter Display name, Name (letters, numbers and underscores; fixed after you save), a Publisher (create your own, because it supplies the prefix) and Version.
  3. Optionally select Set as your preferred solution, so new agents and edits go into it. Without a preferred solution the Common Data Services Default Solution is used.
  • Version only matters when you export: it appears in the exported file name. Solutions can be up to 95 MB. The lifecycle is create, update, upgrade and patch.
  • The solution explorer inherits your security roles; exporting and importing an agent needs at least System Customizer.
  • Other explorer actions: add components, upgrade or update, Remove unmanaged layer (agent ... > Advanced > See solution layers) and Pipelines. Find an agent's solution with View solution in Settings > Agent details.

Add existing agents to a solution

  1. Create (or open) the custom solution.
  2. Add existing > Agent > Agent (the path really says Agent twice) > choose agents in Add existing agents > Add.
  3. In the Objects pane open the agent's ... menu > Advanced > Add required objects, so dependent flows, connection references and environment variables come along.
  4. Export solution (unmanaged for further development, managed for deployment).
  5. In the target environment select Import solution.
  6. Open the agent, configure user authentication again, and publish before sharing it.
  • Components added later (topics, tools, knowledge, environment variables, child agents, MCP servers) don't reach an agent you already exported. Run Add required objects again, re-export and re-import. Prevent the gap by creating agents inside the solution context or with a preferred solution.
  • Add flows with Add required objects; add an environment variable with Add existing > More > Environment variable. Import custom connectors first, before the connection reference and agent solution.
  • If an import fails, Download log file (XML); the usual cause is missing required components. A publish error such as IdentifierNotRecognized points to a missing flow, environment variable or connection reference: add required objects and re-export.
  • A period in a topic name blocks export. Topic and node comments aren't exported. Don't delete topics straight from the solution.
  • Not carried over: Conversation ID, CDS Bot ID, Environment ID and comments. Removing an agent from a solution doesn't remove its components.

Create and use environment variables

An environment variable is a solution component that stores a parameter key and value, so the same agent runs against different values per environment without editing it. Create one in an unmanaged solution: New > More > Environment variable.

Data typeSeen in Copilot Studio as
Decimal numberNumber
TextString
JSONType detected from the value (validation error if it isn't JSON)
Two optionsBoolean (Yes/No)
Data sourceString (a site, list or server parameter, not a credential)
SecretString, read from Azure Key Vault
  • Default Value is used when there is no Current Value; a Current Value wins. A definition has one current value per environment. Clear the current value before export so the target environment supplies its own; values are requested on import and in pipelines. Limit: 2,000 characters.
  • In Copilot Studio variables are read-only; the Variables panel shows their details and the Variable properties panel links to Power Apps, where an admin changes values.
  • Power Fx scope prefix is Environment., alongside System., Global. and Topic..
  • Republish the agent after a value changes, except Secret variables, which are read at run time.
  • A connection reference is a different component: it binds an app or flow to a connection and is set at import.
Environment.PortalBaseUrl & "/tickets/" & Global.TicketId

Secrets come only from Azure Key Vault in the same tenant (register the Microsoft.PowerPlatform resource provider). Grant Key Vault Secrets User to the creator and Dataverse, and for agents also to the Microsoft Copilot Studio Service application. Authorize agents with secret tags: AllowedEnvironments (environment IDs) or AllowedAgents ({envId}/{schemaName}, comma-separated). The runtime caches a secret for 5 minutes (a failed read for 30 seconds). Anyone who can edit the agent could echo the secret in a Message node.

Implement and extend Microsoft Power Platform Pipelines

Pipelines deploy a solution with its connections, connection references and environment variables, not Dataverse data. They deploy managed artifacts only: the artifact exported from your unmanaged development solution passes through the stages in order, and a backup is kept in the host.

Platform host (personal pipelines)Custom host
SetupProvisioned automaticallyAdmin installs the Power Platform Pipelines app in a host environment
ShapeOne development and two target environments; default and Teams environments can't be targetsUp to 7 stages; shared via Deployment Pipeline User / Administrator
ExtendableNoYes
  • Environments: the host and development environments needn't be managed; every target must be managed. From October 2026 an unmanaged target triggers a 30-day notice (plus one 30-day extension) and is then blocked.
  • Run: unmanaged solution in dev > Pipelines > stage Deploy here > Now or Later > Next (preflight) > connection references and environment variables > summary > Deploy. Stages run in order. Makers can cancel until the final step.
  • Gated extensions (custom host): Pre-export Step Required (first stage only), Is Delegated Deployment (approval; the deployment runs as a service principal or the stage owner) and Pre-deployment Step Required.
  • Flows use the Dataverse When an action is performed trigger. Actions: OnDeploymentRequested, OnApprovalStarted, OnApprovalCompleted, OnPreDeploymentStarted, OnPreDeploymentCompleted, OnDeploymentStarted, OnDeploymentCompleted. The flow reports back with UpdatePreExportStepStatus, UpdateApprovalStatus or UpdatePreDeploymentStepStatus and a status code: 10 pending, 20 approved or complete, 30 rejected.
  • Not supported: other tenants, several solutions in one deployment, unmanaged deployments. The default is an Upgrade; you can't pick update. Rollback works only if the pipeline setting that allows redeploying older versions is on.
@contains(triggerOutputs()?['body/OutputParameters/DeploymentStageName'], 'QA')
@equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/OutputParameters/DeploymentPipelineName'], 'Contoso Pipeline')

Trigger conditions like these limit a flow to one stage or one pipeline. The CLI starts a deployment too; all four parameters shown are required:

pac pipeline list --environment {devEnvironmentId}
pac pipeline deploy --solutionName MyAgents --currentVersion 1.0.0.1 --newVersion 1.0.0.2 --stageId {stageId} --wait
Exam traps
  • A managed solution can't be exported, and it can't be imported into the environment that holds its unmanaged source.
  • The solution Name can't change after saving; the Version only shows in the export file name.
  • Agents created without a preferred or current solution go to the Default Solution; a publisher alone changes nothing.
  • Environment variables are read-only in Copilot Studio; a changed value needs a republish, but a Secret doesn't.
  • Pipelines always deploy the managed artifact; targets must be managed, and the Pre-export step applies to the first stage only.
  • Personal pipelines on the platform host can't be extended; approvals need a custom host.

sections.title: Study habits that work
sections.html:
• Build, then read. Do the task in the product first, then read the section to see what you missed.
  • Memorize exact names: menu paths, settings, limits, roles and (for code) object, method and attribute names.
  • Practise the decision, not just the definition. For every feature write "choose it when / do not choose it when".
  • Keep a trap log. Every missed question becomes one line: what I picked and why it was wrong.
  • Use the Missed filter in Quick drill until it is empty, then re-take the full exam.
  • Read documentation dated 2026. Features were renamed and moved between preview and GA recently.

sections.title: Exam-day plan
sections.html:
The week before

  • Take the full timed practice exam twice, a few days apart; fix every skill rated below 4.
  • Skim the cheat sheets and your trap log — do not start new topics.
  • Run the exam sandbox (aka.ms/examdemo) once so flagging, the review screen and the case-study layout are familiar.
  • Online exam? Run Pearson VUE's system test, clear your desk and room and have government ID ready. Test center? Confirm the address and arrival time.
  • Re-check the official study guide in case Microsoft revised the skills list.

During the exam

TopicApproach
PacingWith 40–60 questions in 120 minutes you have roughly 2.0–3.0 minutes per question. Do not spend more than about 3 minutes on one item in the first pass.
First passAnswer what you know, flag what you do not. Answer every question before time runs out — an unanswered item cannot earn credit.
EliminationCross out answers that use retired, renamed or wrong-direction features. Many questions have two plausible options — look for the deciding constraint (GA versus Preview, required role, prerequisite, order of steps).
Multi-selectCount how many answers are requested ("Select TWO"); each must be independently correct.
Configuration itemsCheck the exact setting, scope, role or sequence the requirement names before choosing between similar options.
Case studiesSkim the questions first, then read the scenario for the requirements and constraints that matter. Re-read the exhibit instead of relying on memory. Breaks are allowed in case studies, but you cannot return to questions seen before the break.
Microsoft Learn buttonOn associate and expert exams Microsoft Learn opens in a split screen (no extra time; Q&A, practice assessments and your profile are blocked). Use it only to confirm one detail with Ctrl+F; if you cannot find it in about 90 seconds, make your best choice and flag it.
BreaksThe clock keeps running during a break, and after a break you cannot go back to earlier questions. You cannot break in the middle of a lab or a problem/solution question set. Use the restroom before you start.
ReviewUse the review screen for flagged items. Change an answer only if you can name the specific fact that makes your first choice wrong.
